It exposes three service families: individual subject detail (identifiers, address, authorisation dates, permitted activities, relationships), subject lists by role (analogous to the public listings — this is how you enumerate all platební instituce), and representative relationships. Synchronous XML request/response; WSDL at https://aplc.cnb.cz/jerrsws/ws; WSDL/XSD schemas published (XSD updated 2022-04-21); role, list and activity code tables published as Excel. candidates.why_relevant: Cofidis a.s. is the Czech arm of the French COFIDIS group (parent: COFIDIS, société anonyme, Villeneuve d'Ascq, ID 325 307 106 RCS Lille) and is a ČLFA member. candidates.why_relevant: PlatímPak is Raiffeisenbank's own deferred-payment brand — a squarely on-cell 'bank-owned deferred-payment arm' that was not in the seed list. Product terms are disclosed on-site: purchases up to CZK 25,000, 30 days interest-free, or instalments, provided by a bank under ČNB supervision. Critically it publishes a merchant directory (/seznam-eshopu) and a merchant-acquisition page (/pro-eshopy), plus a media page with brand manual, two logo versions and a named spokesperson (PhDr. Tereza Kaiseršotová). candidates.source_name: Shoptet Doplňky – Platby category (BNPL/instalment addon catalogue)
candidates.why_relevant: The single best pointer source found for this cell. Shoptet is the dominant Czech e-shop SaaS platform and its addon marketplace (403 addons at time of fetch) enumerates, in one place, every payment and deferred-payment provider competing for Czech checkouts: Shoptet Pay, Shoptet Boost (financing), PayPal, Cofidis iPlatba, GoPay+, Comgate, Lemonero (working capital), ThePay, Pays, HomeCredit, PlatímPak, Barion, ESSOX Payments, Skip Pay, Global Payments 2.0, Twisto Pay+, Cofidis Pay Na splátky, Inbank, Smable, Pluxee Flexi, Cashbot Pay, Skip Pay PREMIUM, PayU PREMIUM, Pluxee Gastro. It surfaced three actors absent from the seed brief (PlatímPak, Inbank, Cashbot Pay) and distinguishes standard vs PREMIUM tiers, which is itself a commercial signal.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the /category/platby index and each addon detail page; extract provider name, tier, install/rating metadata if exposed, and first/last seen. Use as the actor-discovery feed that seeds deeper per-provider collection.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning that the dominant e-shop platform's addon store must reveal checkout-technology choices; direct fetch then category snowball

candidates.why_relevant: Czech alternative-financing fintech whose Cashbot Pay product is B2B deferred payment — 'Plaťte svým dodavatelům na třetiny a bez navýšení' (pay suppliers in three instalments at no extra cost) — and which is distributed through the Shoptet checkout catalogue. candidates.why_relevant: Trade association for Czech non-bank finance, explicitly covering 'spotřebitelské úvěry a spotřebitelský leasing' and stating it represents 14 licensed consumer-credit providers. It publishes market statistics, a market-information section, its own annual reports and a press-release stream — the closest thing to sector-level volume data for non-bank consumer credit. Its verified member list is also an actor map for this cell: COFIDIS a.s., ESSOX s.r.o., Home Credit a.s., Twisto Payments a.s., Zaplo Finance s.r.o. and MONETA Auto s.r.o. all appear, confirming Twisto's positioning inside the regulated non-bank finance establishment rather than outside it. candidates.source_name: SOLUS – zájmové sdružení právnických osob (credit registry: member list and debt statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: SOLUS operates Czech client-information registries (registers of individuals, entrepreneurs, creditworthiness and third parties). Two uses for this cell. First, its member list is an actor-discovery feed that surfaced consumer-credit players outside the seed brief: ESSOX s.r.o., Creditstar Czech s.r.o., CreditPortal a.s., PROFI CREDIT Czech a.s., AvaFin Czech s.r.o., Simfina a.s. Second, its aktuality stream publishes hard arrears statistics — e.g. a release dated 30 April 2026 reporting that consumers owe SOLUS members CZK 34.6bn in overdue debt — which is the sector-level credit-quality series against which individual BNPL providers' 'our customers repay on time' claims can be tested.
candidates.legal_status: public association publications; the registries themselves are not public
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of /aktuality/ to capture the recurring arrears statistics releases; semi-annual re-fetch of /clenske-spolecnosti/ as an actor-map refresh. Registry contents themselves are not accessible and should not be pursued.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles reasoning (who audits/aggregates credit behaviour) plus direct fetch

candidates.source_name: Protext submission/client portal (protext.ctk.cz)
candidates.why_relevant: The client-facing side of the ČTK wire. Documents how Czech corporate announcements physically enter the media system: service running since 1999, distribution to 27 Czech news portals and media in nearly 180 countries, guaranteed publication within 4 hours (usually under 2), category targeting, premium portal placement, and monitoring reports at 2h and 48h after publication. Registration is free and one-off submission without registration is possible — which explains why very small payment institutions and fintechs appear on the wire without any newsroom of their own. Useful for modelling distribution latency and for enumerating the downstream mirror portals.
candidates.access_status: public marketing pages; account required to submit
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off documentation read; re-check annually for changes to the mirror-portal list and pricing packages.

candidates.source_name: Sbírka listin — per-entity list of filed documents (annual report, financial statements, auditor's report)
candidates.why_relevant: This is the actual disclosure channel of the cell: for a given subjektId it lists every document filed into the collection of deeds, labelled in Czech with the reporting year — 'účetní závěrka [2024]', 'výroční zpráva [2024]', 'zpráva auditora [2024]', 'zpráva o vztazích [2024]' (related-party report). Confirmed on a bank (Komerční banka, subjektId=68415) with an unbroken 2018–2024 series. For unlisted payment institutions, processors and IT suppliers with no IR page and no press releases, this is the only place revenue, equity, auditor identity and intra-group relations are disclosed. The related-party report is the single best public artefact for mapping which group entities supply which bank.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Per subjektId GET the vypis-sl-firma page, parse the document rows (Czech labels + year in square brackets), then follow ./vypis-sl-detail?dokument={id}&subjektId={sid}&spis={spis} to the PDF. Filings are PDF (often scanned) so pair with OCR + table extraction. Poll annually per entity around the statutory deadline (filing due within 12 months of period end; approval within 6 months), plus a monthly delta sweep for late filers.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from the entity-search HTML: the ./vypis-sl-firma?subjektId= link was extracted from a live IČO lookup, then the deed list itself was fetched and its Czech document labels read

candidates.why_relevant: The statutory beneficial-ownership register — historically the only free way to see who ultimately controls a Czech payment institution, processor or ATM operator behind holding chains. Access now requires login via data box, privileged remote access, or proving legitimate interest to a court.

candidates.source_name: ČNB – Obecný přístup ke stanovení minimálního požadavku na kapitál a způsobilé závazky (MREL) a sekce Řešení krize
candidates.why_relevant: ČNB as resolution authority publishes its general methodology for setting MREL — 2*(P1+P2) for large/systemically important/complex banks earmarked for bail-in, and (P1+P2) + coefficient*(P1+P2) for mid-sized, less complex banks resolved via transfer to a private acquirer — plus transition periods and an aggregate estimate that banks would need to add roughly CZK 120–140bn. ČNB explicitly does not publish bank-by-bank MREL values, so this methodology page is the only public way to reverse-engineer why and when a given Czech bank must come to market with senior non-preferred or subordinated paper. It is the demand driver behind most non-covered bank issuance in this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch the page plus the ČNB news/aktuality feed for revisions ('Revize a doplnění Obecného přístupu k MREL'); hash-diff quarterly.

candidates.why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance's own ownership reporting — explicitly required by this cell. candidates.why_relevant: MF's annual whole-of-market report covering banking, payments, insurance, capital markets and pensions, with structural data and stated policy direction. candidates.source_name: Kancelář finančního arbitra — Výroční zprávy o činnosti finančního arbitra
candidates.why_relevant: Market-safety body squarely inside this cell: the statutory out-of-court dispute resolver for payment services, consumer credit, life insurance, FX and payment-account switching. Its annual report (legally required by 30 June each year) is the only public source that quantifies consumer disputes BY PROVIDER and BY PRODUCT — observed 15,446 proceedings in 2025 with an extraordinary surge in consumer-credit disputes. That is direct, attributable conduct-risk intelligence on named Czech banks and payment institutions. KFA is a state organisational unit funded within the MF budget chapter.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual crawl each June/July of the annual-reports index; also crawl the 'aktuality' feed and the 'platební služby' topic page. Note two hostnames in use (finarbitr.gov.cz and financniarbitr.cz) — normalise on the .gov.cz one.

candidates.source_name: Garanční fond obchodníků s cennými papíry (GFO)
candidates.why_relevant: The second Czech investor-protection safety net alongside GSFT: the guarantee fund for securities dealers, paying 90% of unpaid client assets up to EUR 20,000 on CNB notification. It is the investor-compensation-scheme counterpart to deposit insurance, and completes the market-safety-body map for this cell. Member firms include banks with investment-services licences, so its member list and levy data cross-reference the banking sector.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual crawl of gfo.cz; if the site's own annual-report index proves thin, fall back to the CNB legislative archive and to member firms' own client-information PDFs which restate fund rules, and to or.justice.cz for filed statements.

candidates.why_relevant: The agricultural/forestry state guarantee and subsidised-credit institution — the sector-specific sibling of NRB, established by Government Resolution 337/1993 and registered 16.9.1993. Frequently missed by banking-only source maps.

candidates.why_relevant: Statutory reporting channel that produces documents NOT published on the institutions' own sites. EGAP reports to the Chamber of Deputies on its state-supported activity (observed as twice-yearly in EGAP's own description of its obligations); the CNB submits its financial-result report; and the MF submits information on export insurance and financing with state support under Act 58/1995 Sb. The accompanying budget-committee records and explanatory memoranda often contain forward-looking programme sizing and government intentions before any press release. A full-text search endpoint exists at fulltext.psp.cz.

candidates.source_name: Nejvyšší kontrolní úřad (NKÚ) — kontrolní závěry a tiskové zprávy
candidates.why_relevant: The Supreme Audit Office audits exactly the entities in this cell and publishes full audit conclusions as PDFs plus press releases. Confirmed historical coverage includes an audit of state ownership stakes in commercial companies (K15005), a 2011-era audit of ČEB and EGAP that found imprudent lending and breaches of the Banking Act across nine loans worth CZK 13.2bn, and a more recent audit finding the CNB manages its finances without material errors. NKÚ conclusions are the only public source that contradicts the institutions' own self-reporting, which makes them disproportionately valuable for credibility triangulation. NKÚ's audit mandate over export-support institutions is itself anchored in Act 58/1995 Sb. / Act 166/1993 Sb.

Also track the annual audit plan (plán kontrolní činnosti), which pre-announces which institutions will be audited next year.

negative_findings.description: Only one of the four banks in this cell — Komerční banka — runs a full equity-style IR operation. KB has its own PSE-listed shares and therefore a financial calendar, results presentations, conference calls, a ratings page, a key-figures/fact-book page and a general-meeting record. Česká spořitelna, ČSOB and UniCredit Bank CZ&SK have no listed local equity; their local IR surfaces are thinner and centre on statutory reports plus press releases.
negative_findings.result_summary: Extensive cs and en searching found no local quarterly results presentation deck, no earnings call and no analyst-facing fact book for ČS, ČSOB or UniCredit Bank CZ&SK. The presentation layer for ČS sits at Erste Group and for ČSOB at KBC Group; UniCredit Bank CZ&SK has no equivalent at all beyond UniCredit SpA group reporting.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed four comparable structured IR estates with results presentations, fact books and earnings calendars. That holds only for KB. Any collection design that templates 'four banks, same artefact set' will produce three quarters of empty slots. The correct model is: KB local-complete; ČS and ČSOB local-statutory plus parent-group analytical; UniCredit CZ&SK local-statutory only.

negative_findings.description: Every csob.cz URL attempted this session returned HTTP 500 to WebFetch, across three different paths: /portal/csob/vztahy-k-investorum, /csob/povinne-uverejnovane-informace and /csob/servis-pro-media/tiskove-zpravy.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three of three fetches failed with HTTP 500. The same pages are indexed by search engines with current content, and ČSOB PDFs on /documents/10710/ are reachable in search results, so the site is live and serving. Recorded as a fetch-method problem, not a dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ČSOB Group is one of the three largest Czech banking groups; losing it would gut the cell. The blocker is almost certainly header or user-agent filtering on a Liferay portal rather than a real outage, so a headless browser with realistic headers should recover it. Must not be marked dead on this evidence.

negative_findings.description: All unicreditbank.cz HTML pages attempted returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to WebFetch, both the English and Czech annual-reports pages and the debt investor relations page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two of two fetches returned 403. PDFs on the same domain under /content/dam/cee2020-pws-cz/ are indexed and were surfaced with current content by search, which indicates page-level bot defence rather than an unreachable host.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The document layer is templatable (VZ-YYYY-CZ.pdf, Pololetni-zprava-YYYY-CZE.pdf), so the reports remain collectable via direct asset paths even if the HTML index stays gated. The index page is still needed to discover new filename variants and any prospectus documents.

negative_findings.description: No Czech-language investor-relations landing page could be found for UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia. Czech searches on 'vztahy s investory', 'pro investory' and 'tiskové zprávy' scoped to unicreditbank.cz returned only report PDFs and third-party media coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: Czech-language queries surfaced statutory PDFs and an iROZHLAS tag page, but no unicreditbank.cz IR hub or press-release listing. The only investor-facing page located was English-language Debt Investor Relations.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For this issuer, Czech-language monitoring has to fall back to third-party media and to the Czech editions of the statutory PDFs. There is no local-language IR narrative channel to track, which is itself a finding about how this bank communicates in the CZ market.

negative_findings.description: No RSS, Atom or JSON feed was identified on any of the four banks' IR or press sections.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fetches and searches across kb.cz, csas.cz, csob.cz and unicreditbank.cz surfaced no feed endpoint. KB and ČS both expose dated permalink structures that support diff-based change detection instead; ČS additionally has a JSON-backed document SPA whose backing endpoint may serve as a de facto feed if reversed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection has to be poll-and-diff rather than feed-driven, which raises cost and makes the financial calendars materially more valuable as scheduling inputs. Worth a dedicated check for feed endpoints during the verification pass before committing to polling everywhere.

negative_findings.description: No standalone Pillar 3 / capital adequacy disclosure page was located for any of the four banks, despite targeted Czech searching on 'Pilíř 3' and 'uveřejňování informací'.
negative_findings.result_summary: KB's Povinně uveřejňované informace hub lists six children, none of them a Pillar 3 page; the prudential disclosures appear to be folded into 'Informace o bance' or into the annual report. Equivalent pages for the other three were not reachable or not found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pillar 3 tables are the richest comparable prudential dataset across banks (capital ratios, RWA breakdowns, NPL and forbearance, ESG risk templates). If they are embedded in annual-report annexes rather than published standalone, extraction is a PDF-parsing problem rather than a download problem, which changes the collection design and cost.

negative_findings.description: Max banka a.s. is named in this coverage cell as a live second-tier bank, but it is not one. Czech-language searching established that Max banka merged into its parent Banka CREDITAS, ceasing to exist as a separate legal entity with all contractual rights and obligations transferring to Banka CREDITAS; clients kept account numbers while the bank code moved from 4000 to 2250 with a transitional dual-code period. A direct fetch of maxbanka.eu confirmed the site now presents itself as the 'Max' product line of Banka CREDITAS, and its mandatory-disclosure archive stops at the FY2023 annual report and 30 September 2024 quarterly data. Reporting on the exact timing was not fully consistent across the sources found (the legal merger is reported as effective 1 October 2024, while Banka CREDITAS separately describes completing the Max banka integration during 2025), so the precise date should be confirmed against the Sbírka listin merger deed rather than press coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live independent Max banka disclosure stream exists. maxbanka.eu remains reachable as a frozen historical archive (annual reports 2010–2023, ČBA-format quarterly filings 2021–Q3 2024) and should be harvested once, now, before decommissioning. Ongoing Max-related disclosure belongs to Banka CREDITAS.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheduling Max banka as a recurring source would produce a permanently stale, silently empty feed and would double-count or misattribute volumes that now sit inside Banka CREDITAS. It also means one of the ten named actors in this cell must be reallocated, and that CREDITAS's balance-sheet and client growth must be read as partly inorganic.

negative_findings.description: Hello bank! (operated in the Czech Republic by BNP Paribas Personal Finance SA, odštěpný závod, bank code 3050, Karla Engliše 3208/5, Prague 5) has exited the Czech market. Czech-language searching found that BNP Paribas Personal Finance announced a controlled wind-down of its Czech operations, stopped opening new accounts and offering further products from early April, sent contract terminations to clients, and provided payment accounts and consumer loans only until the end of November of that wind-down year; the stated rationale was that roughly 300,000 clients was below the scale needed to justify further investment against strong competition. A Komerční banka press release was also found recording an agreement to recommend a new contractual relationship to Hello bank's deposit clients. Searching specifically for a 2026 Hello bank Czech press centre returned no such thing.
negative_findings.result_summary: No live Hello bank Czech disclosure or press source exists to track. No Czech statutory annual report exists either, since the entity was an EU single-licence branch (odštěpný závod) rather than a Czech-licensed bank; it is absent from the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Hello bank should be dropped from the live monitoring roster and retained only as a historical case study of challenger-bank exit economics in the Czech market. Its client migration is also a concrete competitive event for the surviving banks in this cell, and the Komerční banka arrangement means the beneficiary sits outside this cell in the top-four cell.

negative_findings.description: Both mBank (mBank S.A., organizační složka, IČO 27943445, Pernerova 691/42, Prague 8 – Karlín, operating in the Czech Republic since 2007) and the former Hello bank operate(d) as branches of EU-licensed banks under the single-licence / mutual-recognition regime, supervised primarily by their home regulator. Fetching the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links confirmed that neither mBank nor BNP Paribas / Hello bank appears among the roughly two dozen banks listed there.
negative_findings.result_summary: There is no Czech-law annual report, no local Pillar 3 filing and no local quarterly disclosure annex for mBank CZ. Its financials are only obtainable inside mBank S.A. Group reporting, where the Czech and Slovak branches are disclosed as a combined line within the Retail Banking segment — meaning Czech-only figures generally must be inferred rather than read off.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any cross-bank comparison table built from Czech statutory disclosures will silently omit mBank, understating challenger-segment share and distorting market-structure conclusions. Collection for mBank must be designed differently from the other eight actors — parent-group segment extraction plus the Czech press portal — and the CZ/SK aggregation must be flagged as a known precision limit rather than resolved.

negative_findings.description: The ČNB list designates https://www.airbank.cz/dokumenty-ke-stazeni as Air Bank's mandatory-disclosure location. Fetching that page returned only forms, contract documents, the price list, the interest-rate overview, business terms, complaint rules and privacy material. No links to annual reports (výroční zprávy), quarterly disclosure annexes or capital-adequacy data were visible on it, even though Air Bank's consolidated annual report PDFs demonstrably exist on the same host under a /file-download/ path.
negative_findings.result_summary: Air Bank's statutory annual reports are retrievable directly by path convention (/file-download/vyrocni-zprava-<YEAR>.pdf, with a numeric-prefixed variant observed for the newest edition) but are not discoverable by crawling the regulator-designated disclosure page. Quarterly and capital-adequacy annexes for Air Bank were not located in this pass at all.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector that trusts the ČNB pointer and crawls only the designated page will conclude Air Bank publishes no annual report — a false negative on one of the cell's most strategically interesting challengers. It also means the regulator's pointer list resolves to a page rather than to a document index, and per-bank crawl rules must be written individually rather than generically.

negative_findings.description: Two priority sources resisted direct fetching in this pass. https://www.creditas.cz/povinne-uverejnovane-informace returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body, while individual PDFs on the same host surfaced normally through search — the signature of bot protection rather than absence. https://www.cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/informace-zverejnovane-emitenty/ (the Central Repository of Regulated Information) ended in a socket hang up, while several sibling cnb.cz pages fetched successfully in the same session.
negative_findings.result_summary: Neither source is recorded as dead. Both are logged as blocked/unverified hypotheses with the observed blocker, and both were routed around: CREDITAS filings are reachable via /files/ document paths and via the Patria regulated-information feed, and the ČNB repository has documented sibling guidance pages that fetched successfully.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recording either as dead on a single bad fetch would drop the cell's most active consolidator and the statutory single point of access for regulated information. It also sets the collection requirement: this cell needs a browser-grade fetcher with realistic headers, not a plain HTTP client, and needs redundant paths designed in from the start.

negative_findings.description: Across the eight domestically licensed banks in this cell, only MONETA Money Bank publishes a genuine quarterly earnings package (presentation, interim report, basic-data spreadsheet, press release, conference-call transcript, webcast video) with an investor calendar and sell-side coverage. Raiffeisenbank CZ produces a country-level investor presentation and half-year financial reports; Fio, Trinity Bank, Partners Banka and formerly Max banka publish only the ČNB/ČBA-format quarterly disclosure annexes, which are regulatory data tables with no narrative, no guidance and no management commentary. Air Bank publishes no local quarterly disclosure that was locatable in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Topic coverage for 'earnings' and 'investor relations' in this cell is structurally asymmetric: one issuer-grade stream, one partial, and the rest data-only. Narrative and forward-looking signal for the non-listed banks has to be reconstructed from press rooms, parent-group reporting and trade press.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Analytical expectations must be set accordingly — quarter-by-quarter competitive narrative is available only for MONETA and partly Raiffeisenbank, and any attempt to build a uniform quarterly comparison across the cell will either fail or silently over-weight the one bank that talks. It also means the annual report and press room carry disproportionate weight for six of the nine surviving actors.

negative_findings.description: Several actor names in this cell are seriously noisy in search and need disambiguation before automated collection. 'Partners' collides hard with Partners Group AG (the Swiss private-markets firm) and its SEC filings, and with 'Partners Group Private Equity' funds — an English-language query for Partners investor materials returned mostly Swiss results. 'Raiffeisen' returns Raiffeisen Bank entities in Serbia, Bosnia and elsewhere plus the Austrian parent, and within the Czech Republic alone spans Raiffeisenbank a.s., Raiffeisen investiční společnost, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna and Raiffeisen – Leasing, each publishing its own výroční zpráva. 'Fio' spans Fio banka, Fio investiční společnost and the Fio brokerage news desk. 'mBank' spans the Polish parent, the Czech branch and the mbank.pl-hosted Czech media portal. 'Trinity' and 'Max' are common words that produce heavy false-positive volume without a bank qualifier.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bare-name queries are unusable for automated monitoring in this cell. Reliable retrieval required pairing each name with Czech disclosure vocabulary ('výroční zpráva', 'povinně uveřejňované informace', 'tisková zpráva') and, for the Raiffeisen and Partners families, with the exact legal form ('a.s.', 'Raiffeisenbank a.s.', 'Partners Banka a.s.').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without name disambiguation rules and an IČO-anchored actor map, a monitoring pipeline for this cell will ingest Swiss private-equity filings as Czech banking intelligence and will conflate a bank with its sister investment company or building society. This is a design requirement for the collection layer, not a cosmetic issue.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch quota (200/200 calls) was already exhausted by other agents before this cell's first query, so no native web search was available at any point during this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Substituted Seznam.cz HTML search (https://search.seznam.cz/?q=...) fetched via WebFetch as the search engine, supplemented by direct HTTP probing and the ARES REST API. DuckDuckGo (both html. and lite. endpoints) served a CAPTCHA challenge instead of results and was not used; the CAPTCHA was not attempted. Mojeek returned HTTP 403. Seznam.cz worked reliably and is, helpfully, the Czech-market search engine, so local-language recall was good — but result depth was limited to roughly the first page per query, and no result-page pagination was possible.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Breadth of discovery for this cell is narrower than it should be. Long-tail actors (smaller PSPs, ISOs, bank-internal processing units) and second/third-page results were systematically not seen. A re-run with search budget available should be assumed to add materially to this slice rather than merely confirm it.

negative_findings.description: The seed query used the Czech phrase 'akvizice karetních transakcí' for card acquiring. In Czech financial usage 'akvizice' means a corporate acquisition (M&A), not card acquiring.
negative_findings.result_summary: That query returned mostly M&A and unrelated legal/broker results, plus a Euronet merchant-acquiring M&A item. The productive Czech terms are the English loanword 'acquiring' used as-is, and native phrasings 'akceptace platebních karet', 'přijímání platebních karet', 'přijímat platby kartou' and 'zpracování karetních transakcí'. Queries rebuilt on those terms returned the relevant acquirers immediately.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated collection built on the seed phrasing will have poor precision and will miss the core actors. The glossary for this cell must treat 'akvizice' as a noisy term and prefer 'akceptace/přijímání platebních karet' plus the bare loanword 'acquiring'.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for a Nexi or Nets Czech-language newsroom, press page or local site.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Czech query 'Nexi Nets Česká republika platební karty zpracování transakcí' returned only homonyms — a Google Play listing for Nexi Business, an unrelated Czech IT firm 'Nexineo CZ', 'Nexnet', and a real-estate agency 'Reality NEXI'. No Czech-language Nexi/Nets corporate presence was found. The company's existence in Czechia was established only via ARES (Nexi Czech Republic, s.r.o., IČO 27391761, V celnici 1031/4, Praha 1, incorporated 2005-10-31) and its Sbírka listin entry.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For Nexi there is effectively no Czech-language disclosure channel: coverage must rest on the statutory filings plus the English group newsroom. Also, 'Nexi' and 'Nets' are both high-noise search tokens in Czech and must always be qualified (with 'platební', 's.r.o.', or the IČO) in any automated query.

negative_findings.description: Looked for a Czech-language press/newsroom page belonging to the legal entities Global Payments Europe, s.r.o. and Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o. themselves.
negative_findings.result_summary: None found. Global Payments' Czech communication runs through the marketing site globalpayments.cz (which serves HTTP 403 to scripted requests) and its blog; there is no 'tiskové centrum' or press-release archive for the Czech entity. Worldline's Czech site (worldline.com/cs-cz/home) is a localised marketing page, with press releases only at group level in English. The historical domain globalpaymentseurope.cz no longer serves the company — a fetch returned a TLS certificate mismatch, the certificate covering the unrelated names 0oo1.cz / www.0oo1.cz.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Czech-entity announcements for the two largest actors in this cell are not separately published. Contract wins and platform migrations affecting Czechia must be caught either at parent-group level in English, in the statutory accounts a year later, or indirectly via the SBK/ČTK wires and trade press. Collection design must not assume a local newsroom exists.

negative_findings.description: Several relevant Czech commercial and aggregator domains refused scripted requests.
negative_findings.result_summary: HTTP 403 observed on www.globalpayments.cz (root, /blog, /podpora/dulezite-dokumenty), www.gpwebpay.cz, www.zivefirmy.cz and the bare host aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz (though the archive path /akt.htm on that host fetched fine). These are hypotheses of bot defence, not evidence of dead sites — all four appear in current search indexes and one served content on a deeper path.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for the Global Payments Czech properties requires a headless browser with a realistic fingerprint; a naive HTTP fetcher will silently report these primary sources as unavailable and the cell will look emptier than it is.

negative_findings.description: Multiple plausible URL patterns for corporate and bank press pages returned errors, indicating site re-architecture rather than absence.
negative_findings.result_summary: worldline.com/en/home/newsroom.html -> 404 (correct path is /en/home/top-navigation/media-relations); worldline.com/en/home/investors.html -> 400 (IR lives on investors.worldline.com); nexigroup.com/en/media/ and /en/media-and-news/ -> 404 (correct prefix /en/media-relations/); investors.globalpayments.com/financial-information/sec-filings -> 404 (correct path /all-sec-filings); csob.cz/portal/o-csob/pro-media and csob.cz/pro-media -> HTTP 500 redirect to an error page; kb.cz/cs/o-bance/tiskove-centrum, rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media and moneta.cz/o-nas/pro-media -> 404; cnb.cz/cs/statistika/platebni-styk/ -> 404 (statistics sit under /cs/statistika/menova_bankovni_stat/harm_stat_data/); protext.cz/zpravy.php and ceskenoviny.cz/tiskove/ -> 404 while the deeper paths work.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per the playbook these are hypotheses, not verdicts. Every one of them was resolved to a live path by re-deriving from site navigation or a fresh search — so any monitoring config must include a re-discovery step on 404 instead of retiring the source. The ČSOB HTTP 500 in particular should be retried before any conclusion.

negative_findings.description: Checked whether the CardMag trade-magazine public PDF archive extends to recent years.
negative_findings.result_summary: The archive index at cardmag.cz/pages/cze/archiv.html enumerates issues in the pattern cm<quarter>_<year>.pdf and the visible listing runs to 2018. Probes for cm2_2025.pdf and cm1_2026.pdf both returned HTTP 404. Whether the magazine ceased, moved behind a member wall, or simply changed its filename scheme was not determined.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CardMag is the deepest narrative source on Czech card processing history, so a truncated archive caps its usefulness for recent-period analysis while leaving it excellent for reconstructing the MUZO/Global Payments Europe lineage and older bank-processor relationships. Worth one targeted follow-up to establish the current publication status.

negative_findings.description: The SBK association site links a members-only data area.
negative_findings.result_summary: http://data.bankovnikarty.cz/secure/private.htm is linked from the SBK home page as a restricted area. It was not accessed and no credentials were sought.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The richest granular Czech card statistics (likely including per-member acquiring data) are behind association membership. Open collection is limited to the published aggregate statistics and quarterly press releases; anything finer would require a legitimate membership or a commercial data agreement, which is a procurement decision rather than a collection one.

negative_findings.description: Two Czech public registers relevant to contract evidence could not be reached from this environment.
negative_findings.result_summary: smlouvy.gov.cz (Registr smluv) timed out twice with zero bytes received (curl exit 28) despite a deep contract permalink appearing as a live indexed search result; vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz failed to connect (HTTP 000). Both are recorded as unverified, not dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The contracts register is one of the highest-value indirect sources for this cell because it exposes actual acquiring contract terms signed by public-sector merchants. Its apparent unavailability is very likely an artefact of this sandbox's network rather than the source, and it must be re-checked from a normal network before any judgement is made about it.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already fully consumed before this cell's first query was issued. BOTH planned cs and en searches ('ComGate platební brána tisková zpráva objem transakcí', 'GoPay platební brána novinky tiskové zprávy e-shop') returned a budget-exhausted notice and performed no search. All 25 candidates in this slice were therefore discovered by direct WebFetch of hypothesised URLs plus link-following and snowballing, not by search-engine discovery.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero successful WebSearch calls. ~30 WebFetch calls executed instead, of which the large majority returned usable content; discovery proceeded by first-principles URL hypothesis + footer/nav link-following + snowballing from press-release contents.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Snowballing from known actors is strong for depth but systematically weak for DISCOVERY of unknown small actors. Long-tail CZ gateways and small e-money institutions that are not linked from any page I fetched are almost certainly missing. The cell should be re-run with search budget available before its coverage is treated as complete.

negative_findings.description: ThePay, a.s. (IČO 28135261, Jihlava) — one of the four named domestic gateway brands in this cell — publishes no blog, no novinky and no tiskové zprávy. Both the homepage (thepay.eu, reached via 301 from thepay.cz) and the contact page were inspected; the footer offers only nápověda, kontakt, pdf-verze and partnerský program.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language terms 'novinky' and 'tiskové zprávy' were searched for on the site and are absent. No press contact published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ThePay cannot be tracked via corporate communications at all. Intelligence on this actor must come entirely from statutory filings (Sbírka listin, IČO 28135261) and third-party trade press. Any collection plan that assumes a press-release feed per gateway will silently produce a blind spot on ThePay.

negative_findings.description: Stripe's newsroom country/language selector was inspected and lists numerous European markets (Poland, Austria, Germany and others) but NO Czech Republic option; no cs-localised newsroom or Czech-specific press content was found. Likewise Adyen's press-and-media page has no regional filtering for Europe/CEE/Czech Republic and is a contact/press-kit hub rather than a dated release archive.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two of the three named international players (Stripe, Adyen) have NO Czech local press room. The third (Revolut) could not be checked because the newsroom returned HTTP 403.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief assumes 'local press rooms of Adyen, Stripe and Revolut Business' exist. For Adyen and Stripe they do not. Their CZ activity must instead be inferred from product/docs surfaces (supported countries, local payment methods, CZK settlement, local acquiring) and from CZ trade press — a materially different and more fragile collection method than press-release monitoring.

negative_findings.description: Two sources expected to carry payment-mix data did not. (1) Comgate's blog contains product announcements and merchant case studies but NO posts on transaction volumes, instant payments, payment-method mix or e-commerce statistics; the only volume reference found was qualitative, in 'Rok 2025 v Comgate' (2026-01-23), which mentions growth in payment volume and client count without figures. (2) Shoptet's press page carries merchant-base growth and Black Friday data but NO payment-method-mix or online-payment-adoption statistics.
negative_findings.result_summary: The 'gateways publish payment mix' hypothesis is only weakly supported. Hard numbers found across the whole cell were sparse and mostly on About/media pages rather than in releases: Comgate 23k e-shops / 10k terminals / CZK 616.6m registered capital / 80 staff / 20 years; GoPay 18k e-shops CZ+SK, 11k merchants Central Europe, CZK 90bn volume target for 2025; Twisto 17k e-shops and 600k users (2019); Besteron 6,100+ clients.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Instant-payment adoption and payment-method mix — two of the highest-value signals this cell was scoped to reveal — are NOT reliably published by the gateways themselves. Those metrics will have to come from ČNB payment statistics, APEK research, or bank-side reporting, meaning this cell should be treated as an actor/merchant-win/product-roadmap sensor rather than as a payment-mix data source.

negative_findings.description: The ČNB open-data page was inspected specifically for downloadable CSV lists of platební instituce and instituce elektronických peněz. The datasets actually enumerated were banks and foreign bank branches, směnárny, non-bank consumer-credit providers and consumer-credit intermediaries. No payment-institution or e-money-institution CSV was listed. Licence terms for reuse were also not stated anywhere on the page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payment-institution open data not confirmed to exist. The JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N endpoint pattern was observed, so other list ids may exist, but this is an untested hypothesis.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cheap open-data path to the CZ payment-institution actor map is not confirmed. The fallback, WS JERRS, requires a commercial certificate and a signed registration request to jerrsws@cnb.cz — a procurement lead time that should be started early rather than discovered late.

negative_findings.description: https://www.revolut.com/news/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body. Per method this is recorded as a bot-defence hypothesis, NOT as a dead source. Whether Revolut operates a cs-CZ localised newsroom, and whether Revolut Business CZ announcements appear there, could not be determined.
negative_findings.result_summary: One of the three named international press rooms is unreadable by plain HTTP fetch and requires a browser-based collector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Revolut is a significant CZ market participant and Revolut Business is directly in scope for merchant acceptance. Leaving this unresolved is a real coverage hole, and the fix (headless browser) is a different collector class from the rest of this slice.

negative_findings.description: Several hypothesised URLs returned 404 or redirected, and are recorded here so they are not mistaken for dead sources: comgate.cz/blog 301 -> comgate.eu/cs/blog which then 404s (the real blog is /cs/blog-o-platebnich-sluzbach); comgate.eu/cs/zminili-se-o-nas 404s although the pro-media page references a 'Zmínili se o nás' media-mentions page (correct slug unknown); cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/seznamy/jerrs/ (trailing slash) 404s; corporate.payu.com/newsroom/ 404s (correct path is /media-and-press/); thepay.cz 301 -> thepay.eu; besteron.cz 301 -> besteron.com/cz/; apl.cnb.cz 301 -> jerrs.cnb.cz.
negative_findings.result_summary: Domain migrations are widespread in this cell — three of the five domestic actors have moved from .cz to .eu/.com domains, and ČNB has moved its register application host.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any historical link list for CZ gateways is likely stale. Collectors must follow redirects and must not treat a 404 on a guessed slug as evidence a section does not exist. The unresolved 'Zmínili se o nás' page in particular is a lost third-party-coverage index for Comgate.

negative_findings.description: IČO/registration identifiers could not be established from the companies' own sites for several in-cell actors: PayU's Czech legal entity name and IČO are absent from czech.payu.com; Besteron's site gives the NBS permit number (ODB-6111/2015-7) and the name 'Besteron A.S.' but no IČO/IČO SK; GoPay's site does not display an IČO for the odštěpný závod. Confirmed identifiers found: Comgate a.s. IČ 279 24 505 / DIČ CZ27924505; ThePay, a.s. IČO 28135261 / DIČ CZ28135261; Skip Pay s.r.o. IČO 07093331; Global payments Europe, s.r.o. (address only).
negative_findings.result_summary: Only 4 of ~8 CZ-relevant entities have a confirmed registration identifier from primary sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The IČO is the join key between the marketing layer (press rooms) and the statutory layer (Sbírka listin, JERRS). Without it, annual reports and licence records cannot be automatically linked to the right brand, and brand-to-entity mapping errors are likely (e.g. GoPay's CZ branch vs its foreign parent).

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget was already fully consumed (200 of 200 calls) before this cell began, so not a single search-engine query could be executed. The mandated cs/en dual-language query sweep — including the supplied seed queries and the extensions prepared for them — was therefore never run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero search-engine queries executed. All discovery was carried out by direct HTTP fetching of hypothesised URLs plus link-following (snowball) from fetched pages, with first-principles reasoning about who must publish, who benefits, who regulates and who aggregates used to generate the initial URL hypotheses. Czech-language coverage was still achieved, but through Czech-language site navigation and Czech terminology in URL construction rather than through Czech-language search queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Snowball-from-known-actors is systematically biased toward incumbents with good websites. It will under-discover small, new or low-web-presence providers, regional media, court and enforcement records, and any actor not linked from a page already visited. The cell's actor map should be regarded as strong on the majors and thin on the tail until a search sweep is run.

negative_findings.description: Cofidis CZ (COFIDIS a.s.) clearly maintains a news/press area — the homepage 'O nás' navigation lists novinky (news) alongside corporate responsibility and awards — but the actual URL could not be resolved.
negative_findings.result_summary: Four candidate paths were fetched and all returned HTTP 404: https://www.cofidis.cz/tiskove-zpravy, https://www.cofidis.cz/o-nas, https://www.cofidis.cz/o-nas.html and https://www.cofidis.cz/cs/o-nas/novinky.html. A sitemap fetch at https://www.cofidis.cz/sitemap.xml also returned HTTP 404.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cofidis is one of the named seed actors and ships two distinct Czech checkout products (iPlatba and Pay Na splátky), so its press channel is materially in scope. Leaving it unresolved is a real gap in the press-release layer for this cell.

negative_findings.description: Raiffeisenbank CZ's media centre could not be located, which matters because its PlatímPak BNPL brand publishes no press releases of its own — platimpak.cz/pro-media offers only a spokesperson contact, two logo versions and a brand manual PDF, and explicitly points readers to the bank's own media centre.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both https://www.rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media and https://www.rb.cz/o-nas/pro-media/tiskove-zpravy returned HTTP 404. The only confirmed rb.cz path found was the privacy page linked from platimpak.cz: https://www.rb.cz/informacni-servis/ochrana-osobnich-udaju, suggesting the site uses an /informacni-servis/ style hierarchy that was not further explored.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: PlatímPak is a bank-owned deferred-payment arm sitting squarely in this cell, and without the parent bank's press channel there is no release-level feed for it at all.

negative_findings.description: Zonky no longer operates as an independent publisher. Its site footer reads '© 2026 Air Bank a.s., člen skupiny PPF, poskytovatel služby Zonky', and its navigation contains no press, media, news or blog section at all — only o-zonky, kontakty, poradna, dokumenty, cenik and an affiliate programme.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed absence of any press/media/news section on zonky.cz. Zonky-related disclosure has migrated upward to Air Bank (which does maintain /pro-novinare/ and /novinky/) and to PPF group reporting.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Zonky is a named seed actor. Any collection design that budgets for a standalone Zonky press feed will silently collect nothing; the routing to Air Bank and PPF must be made explicit in the collection plan.

negative_findings.description: None of the Czech-domiciled specialists in this cell publish annual reports or audited financial statements on their own websites. Home Credit a.s.'s /o-nas page carries a legal-entity identity (IČO 269 78 636, Brno, PPF group, ČNB-authorised as payment institution and non-bank consumer-credit provider) and a client ombudsman, but no reports; ESSOX, Twisto, Skip Pay and PlatímPak similarly expose only terms, pricing and press material.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed across homecredit.cz, essox.cz, twisto.cz, skippay.cz and platimpak.cz: no výroční zpráva or účetní závěrka links found on any of them.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It means the financial-statement layer for this entire cell depends on the Sbírka listin and on foreign parent disclosures (PPF, Home Credit Group, KBC/ČSOB, Inbank Group, Param). Collection design must treat the register as the primary financial source rather than as a fallback.

negative_findings.description: Two important register/statistics endpoints returned essentially no content to a plain HTTP fetch: https://dataor.justice.cz/ returned only the header 'Opendata', and https://www.cnb.cz/arad/ returned only 'ČNB ARAD'. The new unified register portal https://verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz/ rendered only partially.
negative_findings.result_summary: Content is almost certainly assembled client-side. This is a rendering hypothesis, not evidence that the services are unavailable — the ČNB and Ministry of Justice endpoints are official infrastructure and should be assumed live.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These are exactly the machine-readable, licence-clean sources the collection layer should prefer over scraping corporate sites. Getting them working requires a headless browser or the documented data/API endpoints, and that work should be planned rather than discovered late.

negative_findings.description: No Czech trade association, self-regulatory body or code of conduct specific to BNPL or deferred payment was located. The nearest structures found were ČLFA (broad non-bank finance and consumer credit, which does include Twisto Payments a.s. as a member) and SOLUS (credit registries).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched by navigation and by reasoning about who would organise such a body; found none. Czech BNPL providers appear to organise through the general non-bank finance association rather than a BNPL-specific one.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no single BNPL-sector voice publishing volume or conduct data for Czechia, so sector aggregation must be assembled from ČLFA statistics, ČNB supervisory material and APEK e-commerce studies rather than from a dedicated body.

negative_findings.description: Two attempts to reach general search infrastructure and one foreign issuer site were repelled by bot defences.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/ returned a CAPTCHA challenge page ('Please complete the following challenge...', error code 90d2) instead of results, closing off the workaround for the exhausted WebSearch budget. https://www.ipfin.co.uk/en/investors.html returned a page containing only 'Challenge Validation'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that search-engine-based discovery was genuinely unavailable on this pass, and flags IPF as needing a browser-grade fetcher or an RNS-feed route in the collection layer.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200 calls) was already exhausted before this cell's first query was issued, so none of the assigned cs/en seed queries could actually be run. All discovery was performed instead by direct HTTP fetching of known operator domains, HTML link extraction, meta-refresh/redirect following and snowballing (ČNB nav -> CERTIS subpages; SBK homepage -> 531-PDF press archive, CardMag, ČBA; ARES API -> Sbírka listin). Consequently the queries_used fields are legitimately empty rather than fabricated.
negative_findings.result_summary: 0 web searches executed; ~40 direct fetches/status probes executed instead. Coverage of the cell's core actors was achieved, but long-tail recall that keyword search would have surfaced is likely missing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recall risk: sources that are not reachable by guessing a domain or by following a link from an already-known Czech payments site are systematically under-represented in this slice. Re-run the cell with search enabled to close the tail.

negative_findings.description: Mastercard's Czech localised estate refuses automated fetches. https://www.mastercard.cz/cs-cz/o-nas/tiskove-centrum.html and https://www.mastercard.cz/cs-cz/podnikatele/podpora/mezibankovni-poplatky.html both returned HTTP 403 with no body, to WebFetch and to curl with a desktop Chrome user-agent. https://www.mastercard.com/news/europe/cs-cz/ also returned 403.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 on every Mastercard CZ path attempted. Not treated as dead: 403-with-no-body is the classic edge/bot-defence signature, and the domain is still linked as current from Czech trade sites (bankovnikarty.cz, cardmag.cz).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Mastercard is half of the duopoly this cell exists to track. Until a headless-browser collector is in place, Mastercard CZ coverage depends on the SBK/CardMag TZ_MasterCard_*.pdf mirror archive, which is a third-party mirror with unknown completeness.

negative_findings.description: Czech-looking localised paths on visa.cz do not exist: /o-visa/tiskove-centrum.html and /o-visa/novinky.html both return 404. The working Czech newsroom sits on an English path, https://www.visa.cz/about-visa/newsroom.html, while individual releases live under /o-spolecnosti-visa/newsroom/press-releases.NNNNNNN.html — a third path prefix.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two guessed Czech paths 404; the real newsroom (200, Czech-language content) was found by probing the English path. Three inconsistent path prefixes coexist on the same host.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector built on 'localise the path' heuristics will silently miss Visa CZ entirely and may record it as a dead source. Pin the discovered URLs and re-derive detail-page links from the listing rather than constructing them.

negative_findings.description: The acronym APMS (apms.cz), linked from the SBK homepage among payments-industry links, is NOT a payments body. It is the Asociace provozovatelů mobilních sítí — the Czech mobile network operators' association (O2, T-Mobile, Vodafone; IČO 75118891), concerned with telecom infrastructure.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fetched and confirmed off-topic. Excluded from candidates.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Noisy term for this cell: Czech payments sources cross-link telecom bodies (mobile payments context), and an unchecked acronym expansion would pollute the actor map. Flag APMS as excluded in the cell glossary.

negative_findings.description: No Czech-entity annual report, statutory financial statement or CZ-level investor-relations disclosure was found for Visa or Mastercard's Czech operations. Both schemes publish only marketing press releases locally; financial disclosure sits at group level. investor.visa.com and investor.mastercard.com both returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches (bot defence assumed, not verified as dead).
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero CZ-specific scheme financial disclosures located; group IR portals unreachable by automated fetch.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The 'annual reports / investor relations / earnings' topics in this run's scope cannot be satisfied from CZ scheme entities. For scheme economics, the run must fall back to group SEC filings (10-K/10-Q) or to interchange-fee regulatory disclosures, neither of which was located for CZ in this pass.

negative_findings.description: ČNB's oversight page states that PFMI-based assessments of CERTIS (2023, previously 2016) and of the SKD securities settlement system (2023, previously 2018) were completed, but publishes no link to the assessment documents themselves.
negative_findings.result_summary: Assessment existence confirmed in prose; assessment documents not located on the oversight page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The most substantive independent evaluation of the national clearing rail is referenced but not retrievable from the obvious location. Worth a targeted follow-up (ČNB annual report chapters, or an information request) rather than assuming the documents are unpublished.

negative_findings.description: Bankovní identita, a.s. publishes no výroční zpráva (annual report) or financial statements on bankid.cz. The /pro-akcionare/ page held exactly one artefact, a general-meeting ZIP for September 2026, and no shareholder-bank list.
negative_findings.result_summary: Self-published financial disclosure absent; statutory route via Sbírka listin (IČO 09513817, confirmed via ARES) is the only identified path.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bank iD's economics and ownership structure — which banks hold what share of the national identity rail — are only obtainable with the 6-12 month lag of statutory filings, not from the operator's own site. Plan collection accordingly.

negative_findings.description: https://www.praguepaymentsweek.com/ (Czech payments industry conference, linked from both bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz) timed out after 25 seconds with no response.
negative_findings.result_summary: Connection timeout, HTTP code 000. Recorded as unverified, not dead — a single timeout is not evidence of removal, and the site may simply be dormant between editions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Conference programmes are a good pointer source for which scheme and infrastructure topics the Czech industry is prioritising, and for speaker-level actor mapping. Worth a retry from a different network before writing it off.

negative_findings.description: The ČNB ARAD statistical database (https://www.cnb.cz/arad/) is a JavaScript single-page application. A plain fetch returned only the shell 'ČNB ARAD' with no dataset content, so the structure of set D458 (CERTIS statistics, referenced by name from the CERTIS statistics page) could not be inspected, nor could the export formats or any API endpoint be confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Dataset identifier D458 confirmed from the ČNB CERTIS page; dataset contents and export mechanics unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The machine-readable route to Czech clearing volumes is identified but not yet specified. A headless-browser or network-trace pass is needed to capture ARAD's underlying JSON endpoint before this can become an automated feed.

negative_findings.description: Guessed paths that do not exist and should not be re-probed: https://www.cnb.cz/cs/platebni-styk/okamzite-platby/ (404 — the real path is nested under /certis/), https://www.cnb.cz/cs/dohled-financni-trh/vykon-dohledu/dohled-nad-platebnimi-systemy/ (404 — oversight lives at /cs/platebni-styk/oversight/, an English word inside a Czech path), https://cbaonline.cz/tiskove-zpravy (soft 404 page), https://newsroom.mastercard.com/eu/ and /news/eu/en/ (404 — no country-level Mastercard newsroom found).
negative_findings.result_summary: Five plausible-looking paths confirmed non-existent; correct paths recorded in the candidate entries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Documents the dead ends so a later run does not spend budget rediscovering them, and shows that ČNB mixes English slugs ('oversight') into Czech URL trees — path-localisation heuristics are unreliable on cnb.cz too.

negative_findings.description: Both bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz emit malformed links to recent Mastercard press releases, missing the slash after the hostname: 'http://aktuality.bankovnikarty.czTZ_MasterCard_18-08-2026.pdf' and '...czTZ_MasterCard_20-08-2026.pdf'. The equivalent Visa link on the same pages is well-formed and fetches successfully (297 KB PDF).
negative_findings.result_summary: Two current Mastercard TZ links are unfetchable as published; the repaired form is the obvious fix but was not exercised.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive crawler will silently drop the newest Mastercard items from the very archive being used to work around the mastercard.cz 403 — compounding the Mastercard coverage gap. The collector must normalise these hrefs.

negative_findings.description: The SBK and CardMag estates are legacy static sites: the apex URLs serve only a meta-refresh redirect to /pages/czech/home.html and /pages/cze/home.html respectively, content is encoded in windows-1250 rather than UTF-8, the news archive is served over plain HTTP only, and pages carry FrontPage-era markup. WebFetch returned empty content for both apex URLs; only raw curl plus explicit iconv decoding worked.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both sites confirmed live (HTTP 200) and content-rich once the redirect and encoding are handled, but invisible to a standard fetch-and-parse pipeline.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single best CZ card-statistics series and the largest Czech scheme press archive would both be scored as empty or dead by a default collector. Encoding and meta-refresh handling must be explicit for this cell.

negative_findings.description: For the SEPA scheme layer (European Payments Council) and the comparative payments statistics layer (ECB Data Portal), no Czech-language version was found — both publish in English only. No Czech-language SEPA scheme rulebook or Czech national SEPA coordination portal was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: SEPA/EU-level sources are en-only in this slice; the cs-language SEPA layer is unfilled.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The run mandates cs coverage. If a Czech SEPA coordination body or Czech-language rulebook translation exists (plausibly hosted by ČBA), it was not found here and remains an open gap rather than a confirmed absence.

negative_findings.description: The WebSearch tool reported its per-session budget fully consumed (200/200) before this cell's first query, so all discovery had to be routed through WebFetch against public search engines. DuckDuckGo (html and lite endpoints) returned an anti-bot CAPTCHA challenge, which I did not attempt to solve, and Mojeek returned HTTP 403. Seznam.cz (search.seznam.cz) fetched successfully and became the sole discovery engine for this slice.
negative_findings.result_summary: All 16 discovery queries in this slice were executed through search.seznam.cz via WebFetch; ~10 results per query, first page only. No Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo coverage and no deep result pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Seznam's index is strong for Czech-language consumer and corporate content but weaker for English-language financial disclosure, PDF-embedded content and international trade press. Sources findable only via Google/Bing (e.g. ATMIA and international cash-industry publications, English-language CEE ATM market reporting) are systematically underrepresented in this slice, and no result set went past page one.

negative_findings.description: Targeted Czech-language searching for a non-bank ATM deployer other than Euronet ('nebankovní bankomat', 'nezávislá síť bankomatů Česko', 'konkurence Euronetu', 'provozovatel bankomatů', 'nezávislý provozovatel bankomatů v obcích') surfaced no second independent deployer of any scale. Results returned only Euronet properties, Euronet fee criticism, bank ATM listings and map POIs.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Czech IAD competitor to Euronet identified. Euronet's own June 2026 statement — ~10% of all Czech ATMs, ~300 of ~1,200 machines in Prague — is currently the only quantified deployer-share figure found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If confirmed, the Czech independent-deployer market is effectively single-operator, which concentrates the entire non-bank ATM intelligence problem on one company and its parent filings, and makes the Sbírka listin filing of Euronet Services (IČO 25608452) disproportionately important. It also means fleet-share claims come from an interested party with no rival source to triangulate against.

negative_findings.description: The status of G4S's Czech cash business could not be resolved. brinks.cz publishes a post about a partnership with 'G4S Secure Solutions (CZ) a.s.' framed as a security-services cooperation, and two Brink's cash entities are registered in Czechia (Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) a.s., IČO 27590151, incorporated 2006-09-01; Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) s.r.o., IČO 08829969, incorporated 2020-01-08, the latter's incorporation date being consistent with a carve-in around the Brink's–G4S cash transaction period). No document was found confirming whether G4S's Czech cash-in-transit operation was transferred to Brink's, retained, or wound down.
negative_findings.result_summary: G4S Cash Solutions as a distinct Czech CIT operator was not located; only G4S Secure Solutions (CZ) a.s. appears, as a Brink's partner in guarding-type services. Relationship unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Whether the Czech CIT market is a two-player (Loomis/Brink's) or three-player structure changes any read on pricing power and on bank outsourcing leverage. Getting this wrong would misstate the competitive baseline for the entire cash-logistics side of this cell.

negative_findings.description: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (bankovnikarty.cz), historically the canonical publisher of total Czech ATM counts covering the whole estate rather than only bank-operated machines, shows detailed statistics only through roughly 2011–2012 on its Czech market profile page, despite the page carrying a recent 'aktualizováno' stamp.
negative_findings.result_summary: Latest detailed series observed: 10.03m cards, 4,082 ATMs, 69,878 merchant locations, 59,836 POS terminals, with trend data spanning 2001–2011.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This removes the one industry series that historically counted all ATMs regardless of owner. It is the direct cause of the fleet-attribution gap in this cell: ČNB counts bank-operated ATMs only, so without SBK there is no authoritative published split between bank-owned and deployer-owned machines.

negative_findings.description: No published ČNB list of persons authorised to process domestic banknotes and coins (a register of cash-processing companies) was located. The ČNB legislation section yields the Act on the circulation of banknotes and coins, professional-course requirements and the tested-device lists, and portal.gov.cz documents an information-provision duty toward ČNB, but no public roster of processors was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found instead: two device registries (banknote and coin processing equipment) and a gov.cz service page describing reporting to ČNB. No entity-level register of cash processors surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A processor register would be the cleanest possible census of the Czech cash-handling industry, including small and regional operators invisible to media and to financial-sector lists. Its absence forces reliance on CZ-NACE sweeps in ARES and on security-industry association directories, both noisier.

negative_findings.description: Four fetches failed and are recorded as hypotheses, not verdicts: ir.euronetworldwide.com (landing page and /news-events/press-releases) and investors.brinks.com both timed out at 60s; smlouvy.gov.cz search UI timed out at 60s; www.sec.gov EDGAR browse-edgar returned HTTP 403.
negative_findings.result_summary: None of these was confirmed dead. The SEC 403 is the expected response to a request without a compliant declared User-Agent under SEC access policy; the timeouts are consistent with CDN/bot defence or slow server-side rendering. smlouvy.gov.cz content was independently observed as indexed and reachable via search results (individual contract URLs appeared).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These four are among the highest-value disclosure endpoints in the cell. Recording them as dead would wrongly drop parent-level and contract-level intelligence; the correct next step is a fetch with a declared User-Agent and longer timeout, or use of the documented APIs and open-data dumps rather than the web UIs.

negative_findings.description: No Czech-language term, association or portal specific to cash-in-transit or ATM deployment as an industry was found. Searches on 'převoz cenin', 'komora podniků komerční bezpečnosti', 'asociace bezpečnostních služeb' returned only the general commercial-security chamber KPKB ČR and allied bodies, whose published partner list did not include Loomis, Brink's, G4S or Securitas.
negative_findings.result_summary: Czech CIT appears to have no dedicated sectoral association or trade portal; it sits inside the broader commercial-security industry vocabulary ('ostraha majetku a osob', 'převoz cenin', 'bezpečnostní služby').
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no single local-language hub to snowball from for cash logistics, so actor discovery for smaller CIT firms must come from CZ-NACE sweeps in ARES, procurement award notices and security-association member directories rather than from an industry body.

negative_findings.description: No Czech Banking Association API standard or open-data feed for ATM and branch locations was found. Searching in Czech for 'standard API bankomaty pobočky open data lokality' returned only consumer directories (banky.cz, penize.cz, airbank.cz map pages), with the engine explicitly flagging that results did not contain the API/association/open-data terms.
negative_findings.result_summary: No PSD2-style or association-standard ATM-locator open dataset located for Czechia in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A standard locator feed would give exact, operator-attributed fleet data at near-zero collection cost. Without it, fleet mapping falls back to OpenStreetMap extracts and sampled directory scraping, which are less complete and carry licensing constraints.

negative_findings.description: No bank–ATM operator outsourcing contract or announcement was found in Czech-language searching ('banka outsourcing bankomatů smlouva Euronet MONETA Raiffeisenbank provoz sítě'). Euronet markets 'Outsourcing bankomatů' and 'Dohoda o účasti v síti' on its own /banky/ page, but no counterparty bank was named in any public source located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Outsourcing offer confirmed on the deployer side; no named Czech bank counterparty found in public sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bank-to-deployer outsourcing is the single most consequential structural variable in this cell — it determines how much of the bank fleet is really deployer-run. That it is undisclosed on both sides means it must be inferred indirectly (Sbírka listin narratives, related-party notes, procurement records, field observation of operator branding on machines).

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget was already fully consumed (200 of 200 calls) before this cell began. Every planned Czech-language and English seed query — 'Asseco Central Europe tiskova zprava banka implementace', 'Trask Solutions pripadova studie banka reference', and the remaining seed and extension queries — was refused by the tool with a budget message, not executed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero search queries executed. All discovery in this slice was performed by direct URL fetching of seed-actor domains, sitemap enumeration, redirect-chain following and navigation snowballing. The queries_used field is therefore empty on every candidate — this is an honest empty, not an omission.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The routine mandates local-language search. Fetch-and-snowball recovers the known actors and their structures well, but it cannot surface unknown vendors, one-off press releases carried only by third parties, or bank-project stories on sites nobody thought to guess. Recall in this cell should be assumed materially below what a searched run would achieve, and the cell should be re-run with search budget available.

negative_findings.description: The coverage cell pairs 'Aricoma/Cleverlance' as one actor. A fetch of https://www.cleverlance.com/ returned HTTP 301 to https://www.avenga.com/ — not to Aricoma. Avenga's own site lists Prague, Brno and Ostrava offices and financial clients including Raiffeisen Bank, UniCredit, Generali and Fidelity.
negative_findings.result_summary: Cleverlance's web identity now resolves to Avenga, a separate group from Aricoma/KKCG. Aricoma (aricoma.com, KKCG technology division) is a distinct live actor with its own newsroom and customer wall.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Treating Cleverlance as an Aricoma sub-brand would silently drop a whole delivery organisation with substantial Czech banking history from the monitored set, and would mis-attribute past Cleverlance bank projects to the wrong corporate parent. Both aricoma.com and avenga.com must be tracked separately.

negative_findings.description: Trask appears to have retired its Czech-language web presence. https://www.trask.cz/ issues a 301 to https://www.thetrask.com/, and both https://www.thetrask.com/cs and https://www.thetrask.com/cz returned HTTP 404. All observed navigation and content paths use the /en/ prefix.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Czech-language Trask site path was found. Trask content is collected in English only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Trask is the single richest source of Czech bank project disclosure in this cell, yet it now publishes in English only. Anyone monitoring by Czech keywords alone will miss it entirely, and Czech-language name variants of banks (e.g. 'Ceska sporitelna' vs 'Ceska Sporitelna'/'CS') will not match. Monitoring rules for Trask must be English-keyword-based, which is the opposite of the default assumption for a Czech vendor.

negative_findings.description: CCA Group (cca.cz) is live and well-structured in Czech, but its published reference set contains no banking or financial-institution clients. Observed references are the Ministry of Justice (information systems since 1995), the Czech Office for Surveying and Cadastre, the Ministry of Finance gambling-oversight system AISG, and SKODA JS ERP.
negative_findings.result_summary: CCA Group verified as a live actor but not currently a bank-technology disclosure channel; it reads as a public-sector and industrial custom-software house.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell definition assumes all ten seed vendors are bank-technology suppliers. At least one is not, on its own public evidence. Spending equal crawl budget across all ten would waste effort; CCA should drop to low-frequency keyword-triggered monitoring rather than routine collection.

negative_findings.description: Aricoma's press-release stream carries no banking items in its recent output. The three most recent releases observed on both the EN (/press-releases) and CS (/cs/tiskove-zpravy) indexes are the Dentsu Tracking acquisition (01/08/2026), the acquisition of SAP suppliers in Austria and Slovenia (08/01/2026) and the consolidation of its SAP companies (01/01/2026). Separately, the /case-studies index exposes a 'Banks and Insurance Companies' branch filter but the default listing surfaced no banking case studies among 20+ visible items.
negative_findings.result_summary: Aricoma's banking relationships are visible on its customer wall (CSOB Group, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, ING, Citibank) but are not narrated in recent press releases or in the unfiltered case-study listing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For Czech bank projects Aricoma discloses relationships, not projects — the customer wall carries the signal while the newsroom carries M&A. Collection should weight the customer wall and the filtered case-study view over the press feed, and the filtered branch view must be fetched explicitly because the default listing hides it.

negative_findings.description: Asseco properties refused plain HTTP fetches. https://ce.asseco.com/ and https://ce.asseco.com/en/news/ both returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body; https://asseco.com/investor-relations/ and https://inwestor.asseco.com/en/ likewise returned 403. The legacy domain https://www.asseco-ce.com/cz/ returned a 302 to ce.asseco.com, confirming an intentional, maintained domain migration.
negative_findings.result_summary: Asseco Central Europe and Asseco Poland IR are recorded as unverified-blocked, NOT dead. A maintained 302 from the legacy domain is positive evidence the estate is live and actively managed; a blanket 403 across four unrelated paths on two hosts is the signature of a WAF, not of removed content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Asseco Central Europe is arguably the most important single actor in this cell — a core-banking supplier across CZ/SK whose parent is WSE-listed and therefore subject to audited segment disclosure. Losing it to a premature 'dead' verdict would gut the cell. Re-attempt with a headless browser; if the issuer site stays blocked, route to the regulated WSE/ESPI filing channel, which is the more durable path regardless.

negative_findings.description: GEM System could not be characterised. Four URL variants — https://www.gemsystem.cz/, https://gemsystem.cz/, https://www.gemsystem.cz/cz/ and https://www.gemsystem.cz/robots.txt — all terminated with 'too many redirects (exceeded 10)'.
negative_findings.result_summary: GEM System recorded as unverified with a redirect-loop blocker. The host resolves and responds at every variant, so the site is very likely live; the loop pattern is characteristic of www/non-www or locale negotiation failing against a cookieless client.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: One of ten seed actors is entirely uncharacterised, so its banking references (if any) are unknown. The failure mode is a client limitation rather than a source problem, which means it is cheaply fixable with a cookie-enabled headless fetch — it should not be written off.
