negative_findings.description: Two high-value branches of the BCPP bulk server returned HTTP 401 Unauthorized on directory listing: http://ftp.pse.cz/Issuers.dta/ (probable issuer master data) and http://ftp.pse.cz/Vestnik.doc/ (Burzovní věstník, the official exchange gazette). Sibling branches on the same host (Annual.rep, Semiannual.rep, Info.bas, Statist.dta) listed normally over plain HTTP.
negative_findings.result_summary: 401 on both; recorded as bot-defended-or-gated hypotheses, not as dead sources. Not retried with a browser user-agent or over https within this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The Věstník is the legally authoritative, dated record of admissions, suspensions and exclusions — precisely the artefact that makes the exchange channel valuable when an IR page is later edited. Losing it forces reliance on the softer /novinky items and on ČNB OAM.

negative_findings.description: Across all four BCPP equity segments there is currently no Czech listed pure-play payments or fintech issuer. Banking equity exposure is three names (Komerční banka, Moneta Money Bank, Erste Group Bank, all Prime). The nearest payments exposure is SAB Finance (Standard Market, CZ0009009940, FX/payment services) and WAG Payment Solutions/Eurowag (Free Market, GB00BLGXWY71 — a UK-incorporated dual listing whose primary regulated disclosure is not Czech). The START roster at scan time (BEZVAVLASY, EMAN, FILLAMENTUM, FIXED.ZONE, HARDWARIO, M&T 1997, M2C, MMCITÉ, PILULKA LÉKÁRNY, PRABOS PLUS) contains no fintech; EMAN is the only software house with banking-adjacent work.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed by reading all four segment lists directly; Czech-language search on 'trh START fintech platební společnost IPO' surfaced only general START/IPO commentary and no fintech listing in 2024–2025.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed START would capture smaller fintechs that bank lists miss; at present it does not. The bond channel, not the equity channel, is where the Czech banking sector actually shows up on this venue — which reweights collection towards the debt-securities lists and the ČNB OAM.

negative_findings.description: Guessed URL https://www.pse.cz/en/market-data/bonds/prime-market returned HTTP 404. The real path for debt instruments is /en/market-data/debt-securities/{corporate-sector|financial-sector|public-sector|other-debt-securities}. Separately, https://www.cdcp.cz/index.php/cz/11-emitenti-a-administratori (surfaced by search) returned 404 on fetch, and https://www.pse.cz/en/issuer-guide failed the fetch tool's domain safety check on one attempt while other pse.cz pages fetched normally in the same run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as URL-structure/transient findings, not as dead sources — the CDCP issuers page almost certainly moved during a site restructure, and the pse.cz safety-check failure was inconsistent within the same session.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A verification pass that treats these as dead would wrongly drop two live sources. It also shows that BCPP does not mirror its equity URL structure for bonds, so a collector must be told the debt paths explicitly.

negative_findings.description: Several BCPP pages return only navigation chrome to a plain HTML fetch and load their substance client-side: the Event Calendar (/en/event-calendar), the news listings (/novinky, /en/news — the fetch showed a 'Nahrávám' loading state), the per-issuer News tab (/en/detail/{ISIN}?tab=news returned no headlines), and the Official Price List filtered view.
negative_findings.result_summary: Confirmed on four separate fetches. Static content (market-data segment lists, rules pages, press page, ftp listings) fetched fine.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets the technical floor for this cell: a headless-browser or endpoint-level collector is required for the time-sensitive announcement and calendar surfaces, while the roster and archive surfaces can be collected with simple HTTP.

negative_findings.description: A BCPP staging/test host, tst22.pse.cz, is publicly reachable and indexed by search engines, serving apparently complete copies of issuer detail pages and FAQ pages (e.g. tst22.pse.cz/detail/CZ0009011086, tst22.pse.cz/detail/CZ0009011920, tst22.pse.cz/faq-investor-obchodovani). The ftp server likewise exposes TESTIssuers.dta and TESTresults branches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Observed repeatedly in search results across three separate queries. Not fetched or relied upon.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Do NOT collect from tst22.pse.cz: staging content is unversioned, may be stale or synthetic, and using it would corrupt provenance for a channel whose whole value is authoritative timestamping. Flagged so a crawler configuration explicitly blocklists the host rather than treating it as a convenient mirror.

negative_findings.description: No permanent per-issuer announcement archive URL was found on pse.cz. The issuer detail page's News block links out to the site-wide /en/news search rather than to a filtered, stable per-ISIN announcement history, and no 'regulated information' section distinct from the general news feed exists on the exchange site.
negative_findings.result_summary: Checked the Czech and English KB pages, the Moneta news tab and the news landing pages; the only route to an issuer's history is a keyword query (e.g. "Komerční banka") against the general news search, which mixes BCPP notices with ČTK newswire items.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Per-issuer historical reconstruction on the exchange channel depends on keyword search quality and on the PSE/ČTK source flag being captured correctly; for authoritative per-issuer history the ČNB OAM repository must carry the load instead.

negative_findings.description: No established Czech-language term or dedicated BCPP page was found for an exchange-side 'delisted / former issuers' register. Czech searches using 'vyřazené emise', 'vyloučení emise z obchodování' and 'vyřazení z obchodování' returned only individual news items (e.g. the AVAST exclusion from Free Market on 24 February 2022, ISIN GB00BDD85M81; the JUVENTUS F.C. suspension and re-listing under a new ISIN after a reverse split) rather than a consolidated list.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language coverage was attempted and produced item-level results only; the consolidated register does not appear to exist publicly under any term I could find.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical issuer-universe reconstruction (which Czech financial-sector companies once carried disclosure duty) cannot be done from a single BCPP page and will have to be assembled from dated news items, the Věstník (currently 401), or CDCP records.

negative_findings.description: ČNB's Otevřená data page exposes exactly seven datasets (banks and branches of foreign banks, exchange offices, non-bank consumer credit providers, independent credit intermediaries, tied credit representatives, tied credit intermediaries, foreign credit intermediaries). There is NO open dataset for platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, poskytovatelé platebních služeb malého rozsahu or vydavatelé elektronických peněz malého rozsahu.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk CSV/JSON access covers the banking and credit-intermediation side only; the payments population must be obtained by scraping JERRS, by using WS JERRS with a certificate, from the ČNB PSRI statistical list, or from the EBA PSD2 register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The payments half of the sector — the fastest-changing population and the one most relevant to a payments market-intelligence programme — has no frictionless machine-readable feed from the national regulator. Collection design must not assume symmetry with the banking datasets.

negative_findings.description: WS JERRS, the only official API over the register of regulated entities, requires a commercial certificate from an approved CA and an electronically signed access request emailed to jerrsws@cnb.cz before any call can be made.
negative_findings.result_summary: No anonymous or key-based access exists; provisioning is a manual, paperwork-bound process with an unknown lead time.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cleanest entity feed cannot be switched on in a research sprint. Either budget for the certificate and application process up front, or design the pipeline around HTML scraping plus the seven open-data CSVs from day one.

negative_findings.description: A guessed JERRS deep link (https://jerrs.cnb.cz/apljerrsdad/JERRS.WEB10.HLEDANI_SUBJEKTU?p_lang=cz) returned HTTP 500. The ČNB applications are Oracle PL/SQL web apps whose procedure names and parameters are not documented publicly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hypothesis, not a verdict: the entry points that were actually observed (JERRS.WEB07.INTRO_PAGE, JERRS.WEB45.LOGIN_A, SIPRESWEB.WEB21/WEB_PROSPECTUS/WEB_SHORTSELL.START_INPUT_OAM) responded, so the apps are live; only the invented procedure name failed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collectors must navigate from the ČNB short-links (/cnb/jerrs, /cnb/registr_prospektu, /cnb/kratke_pozice_cz) and follow redirects and forms rather than hard-coding internal procedure URLs, which will break or 500 without notice.

negative_findings.description: Several fetches of www.cnb.cz returned ECONNRESET, 'socket hang up', or a domain-safety block from the fetching layer, while the same or adjacent URLs succeeded on retry.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as transient network/bot-defence behaviour, NOT as evidence that any ČNB URL is dead. All ČNB URLs recorded here are unverified for liveness by design and must be confirmed by the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive liveness checker will mark ČNB pages dead on first failure and prune the single most important source cluster in the whole CZ landscape. Retries with backoff and a realistic user agent are required.

negative_findings.description: For the ČNB Registr prospektů it could not be confirmed from the register's own page whether the full prospectus PDFs are hosted and downloadable from ČNB, or whether the register carries only metadata plus a reference to the issuer's own publication. ČNB explicitly states that publication in the list does not replace the issuer's publication duty under Regulation (EU) 2017/1129.
negative_findings.result_summary: Open question requiring a hands-on retrieval test against a known Czech bank base prospectus.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Determines whether the prospectus collector is a document harvester or only a metadata index that must then be joined to issuer websites — a materially different build.

negative_findings.description: The European Single Access Point, which is intended to aggregate national OAM content including the ČNB Central Storage, is not yet a usable source: collection from collection bodies is scheduled to begin around July 2026 with public access targeted for July 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2023/2859.
negative_findings.result_summary: ESAP cannot be used as a substitute for scraping the ČNB OAM in the current run; it is a watch item, not a source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids designing the CZ disclosure collector around an access point that will not deliver data in this planning horizon, while flagging a foreseeable migration that will reduce scraping cost later.

negative_findings.description: Two local-language pitfalls were observed. First, the bare phrase 'seznam ČNB' is heavily reused by commercial finance portals (finanza.cz, penize.cz and similar) that republish ČNB register extracts, so it retrieves mirrors rather than the primary source. Second, 'OAM' is not Czech usage — it is the EU 'officially appointed mechanism' concept surviving only in the oam.cnb.cz hostname; the Czech public name is 'centrální úložiště regulovaných informací'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches must use the full Czech official names; the acronym OAM is useful only for URL pattern matching, not for Czech-language retrieval.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design that relies on acronyms or short forms will surface secondary aggregators and mis-attribute authority, contaminating a source register meant to record primary sources.

negative_findings.description: No robots.txt, terms-of-use or re-use licence was read for www.cnb.cz, oam.cnb.cz, jerrs.cnb.cz, or.justice.cz or pse.cz during this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Legal status recorded for each candidate is inferred from the public-register character of the sources and, for the ČNB open data, from the explicit open-data regime under nařízení vlády č. 425/2016 Sb. — not from a read licence document, except where stated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection at scale should be gated on an explicit robots/ToS check per host before the collectors go into production, particularly for or.justice.cz and pse.cz which are not open-data publishers.

negative_findings.description: Free public access to the Czech beneficial-ownership register (Evidence skutečných majitelů) was withdrawn. The Ministry of Justice announced that from 17 December 2025 the public part of ESM and its open data are unavailable, citing Czech Supreme Court / Supreme Administrative Court and CJEU case law on disproportionate interference with privacy and the transposition of the new EU AML package.
negative_findings.result_summary: esm.justice.cz still responds, but the freely searchable public extract and open-data distribution that this cell relied on for ultimate-ownership mapping are no longer available to an unauthenticated researcher; access now requires data-box login, privileged remote access, an AML-obliged-entity form, or proof of legitimate interest before a court.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ownership of Czech payment institutions, processors and ATM/IT vendors is frequently held through layered holdings; without ESM the register only shows the registered shareholder, so ultimate control must now be inferred from úplný výpis history, related-party reports in the deeds collection, or bought from commercial databases.

negative_findings.description: The Ministry of Justice open-data catalogue (dataor.justice.cz) is a client-side React application whose datasets are served through CKAN-style endpoints discovered in its JavaScript bundle: /api/3/action/package_list_compact, /api/3/action/package_show and /api/file/.
negative_findings.result_summary: Calling /api/3/action/package_list_compact without parameters returned HTTP 400 with a zero-byte body, and /api/3/action/package_show?id=full returned 'MissingObject{type=ShowResult, id=full}'. The correct dataset identifiers and query parameters were not determined in this run; they are documented in the 81-page ISVR open-data user manual (sections 3-4) which was downloaded but not fully read.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the only bulk, non-rate-limited path to the whole Czech register; until the parameters are worked out, the actor-universe build stays dependent on the rate-limited and CAPTCHA-protected or.justice.cz web UI.

negative_findings.description: No bulk or API distribution of the Sbírka listin documents themselves (the annual report / financial statement PDFs) was found. The ISVR open data covers register entries — the user manual's structure is organised by legal form and its mandatory/optional attribute sets (s.r.o., a.s., družstvo, nadace, SVJ...), i.e. subject data, not filed documents.
negative_findings.result_summary: The documents appear to be reachable only per entity, through or.justice.cz/ias/ui/vypis-sl-firma?subjektId={id} and then vypis-sl-detail?dokument={id}&subjektId={id}&spis={id}.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collecting the disclosures at scale therefore requires an entity-by-entity crawl inside the ministry's published limits (3000 requests/day, 50/minute, random CAPTCHA), which shapes the whole collection architecture and argues for a licensed commercial mirror as a complement.

negative_findings.description: The ISVR open-data usage terms (dataor.justice.cz/files/ISVR_OpenData_Podminky_uziti.pdf, v1.0, 4 March 2019) permit users to disseminate, use and cite the data and to use it 'pro nekomerční použití' (for non-commercial use), and state that the distribution contains personal data so the recipient becomes a data controller under GDPR.
negative_findings.result_summary: The same document states the distribution is neither a copyright-protected database nor protected by the sui generis database right, so its structure and content may be freely extracted and reused — but the non-commercial usage wording and the GDPR controller status are unresolved for a commercial market-intelligence programme.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A commercial intelligence product built on bulk ISVR data may exceed the stated licence; this needs legal review before ingestion, whereas per-entity public register lookups and ARES API use are not covered by that clause.

negative_findings.description: Three candidate URLs failed on first probe and were recovered rather than recorded as dead: https://csu.gov.cz/registr-ekonomickych-subjektu returned 404 (RES application recovered at https://apl.czso.cz/irsw/); a deep link into rzp.gov.cz (/verejne-udaje/cs/udaje/vyber-subjektu.html) failed to connect (working root https://rzp.gov.cz/); https://www.hlidacstatu.cz/api/v2/doc returned 404 while the live documentation sits at /api/v1/doc. Separately https://www.dnb.com/cs-cz.html returned 404 while https://www.dnb.com/cs-cz/ resolved, and bisnode.cz / albertina.cz both redirect there (rebrand, not death).
negative_findings.result_summary: All five were recovered to working equivalents via root/nav or entity research; none is a genuinely dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Documents the recovery ladder outcomes so a later verify pass does not re-flag these as broken, and records the Bisnode->Dun & Bradstreet rebrand for entity resolution.

negative_findings.description: Two Czech term collisions were observed during searching. 'ARES' resolves both to the official Ministry of Finance system at ares.gov.cz and to an unrelated private look-alike at ares.cz (plus aresgov.cz). 'Sbírka' is ambiguous: 'sbírka listin' (collection of deeds) versus 'e-Sbírka' / 'Sbírka zákonů' (the collection of laws at zakony.gov.cz), which surfaced in results for a deeds-related query.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries mixing 'sbírka' with 'API/otevřená data' pulled e-Sbírka legal-code results; queries for 'ARES' pulled the private mirror above the official system.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Both terms need disambiguators ('sbírka listin' + 'obchodní rejstřík'; 'ARES' + 'ares.gov.cz' or 'ekonomické subjekty') or the collection pipeline will ingest the wrong corpus or cite an unofficial mirror as the official register.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted partway through this cell, after which no further WebSearch queries could be issued.
negative_findings.result_summary: Planned follow-up searches — notably Czech-language searches for the ČNB list of licensed payment institutions, for 'výroční zpráva a účetní závěrka uložená do sbírky listin 2025 platební', and for bulk deeds-download tooling — were not run as searches. Affected sources were instead reached by direct URL probing and by snowballing links out of already-fetched pages, so ČNB's JERRS register is recorded on a direct probe alone rather than on search evidence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell is grounded but not exhaustive; a follow-up run with search budget should re-run the unexecuted seed queries, especially the 2025-specific filing query.

negative_findings.description: The new ministry portal verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz (announced on or.justice.cz as running in 'ověřovací provoz') is a Nuxt application whose search runs client-side; its deep-link route scheme was not determined.
negative_findings.result_summary: Guessed routes /vyhledavani, /vyhledat, /sbirka-listin and /subjekt/{ico} all returned 404, while the root and the /clanky/... article pages responded. Its client state exposes three search scopes (publicRegister, trusts, realOwners).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: When the legacy or.justice.cz URL patterns are retired, the whole deeds-collection crawler must be re-pointed; the replacement URL scheme is still unknown and needs a headless-browser session to capture.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for a national aggregator of covered-bond investor reports / cover-pool data (terms: 'kryté dluhopisy', 'krytý blok', 'evidence krytých bloků', 'seznam emitentů', ČNB Vyhláška č. 2/2019 Sb. o evidenci krytých bloků). ČNB maintains the register of permitted covered blocks and labelled ISINs, and issuers must regularly report to ČNB on compliance, but no public Czech portal publishes the underlying cover-pool data.
negative_findings.result_summary: No national HTT/cover-pool portal exists for CZ. Cover-pool disclosure is issuer-by-issuer (KB, UniCredit CZ&SK, MONETA, Česká spořitelna) plus the pan-European Covered Bond Label. The ČNB register gives issuer names, LEI/IČO and ISINs only — no pool composition, LTV, OC or arrears data.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for this cell cannot be centralised on one regulator feed. The pipeline must fan out to six issuer sites (some bot-defended) and to coveredbondlabel.com, and must treat the ČNB list as the completeness check rather than the data source.

negative_findings.description: Plain HTTP fetches to several Czech bank disclosure hosts were refused: unicreditbank.cz returned HTTP 403 on both /cs/o-bance/dluhopisy-prehled.html and /en/ostatni/debt-investor-relations.html; creditas.cz returned 403 on /o-bance/pro-investory; csob.cz returned HTTP 500 on /csob/povinne-uverejnovane-informace; csobhypotecni.cz returned HTTP 500 on /o-bance/emise-hzl and /o-bance/zpravy-o-hospodareni-dokumenty/.
negative_findings.result_summary: Four issuer hosts are unreadable by simple fetch, yet PDF documents on the very same hosts are indexed and referenced from search results, which strongly suggests bot defence / edge-WAF behaviour rather than dead pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is a hypothesis, not a verdict — none of these should be recorded as dead. The collector for this cell needs a headless-browser tier with realistic headers for HTML index pages, while direct GET on /content/dam/, /documents/ and /files/ PDF paths appears sufficient for the documents themselves.

negative_findings.description: coveredbondlabel.com issuer pages and the issuer directory were fetched statically. The Komerční banka issuer page (id 177) rendered its contact list, pool programme list, bond list and HTT section all as '0-10 of 0', and /issuers/directory rendered an empty filter table. /issuers and /national-information both returned HTTP 404.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Label's Czech data exists but is client-side rendered; static scraping yields empty tables and would falsely suggest Czech issuers publish nothing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A naive collector would record the three labelled Czech issuers as having no HTT filings. Headless rendering is mandatory here, and the correct paths are /issuers/directory, /issuers/national/list, /new-htt and /htt-database.

negative_findings.description: Raiffeisenbank a.s. (covered blocks RBCZ_BLOCK_02 and RBCZ_BLOCK_03, with labelled issue XS3019003253) and Hypoteční banka (HB-Blok 4) both appear in the ČNB covered-block register, but Czech- and English-language searching surfaced no dedicated public cover-pool/HTT/investor-report page for either. RBCZ's securities page references an 'International Covered Bonds Programme' without a linked cover-pool report; Hypoteční banka's trail is prospectus/emisní-dodatek only. Neither was found among Covered Bond Label issuers (KB, UniCredit CZ&SK and Česká spořitelna were the three identified).
negative_findings.result_summary: Two of six licensed Czech covered-block issuers have no located public cover-pool disclosure surface.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cover-pool coverage for CZ is structurally incomplete: any CZ-wide covered-bond comparison built from public sources will be missing Raiffeisenbank and Hypoteční banka, which must be flagged rather than silently treated as zero.

negative_findings.description: No settled Czech-language term for 'senior non-preferred' was found in issuer or regulator material. Czech sources use descriptive constructions — 'nepodřízené dluhopisy', 'podřízené dluhopisy', 'MREL dluhopisy', 'způsobilé závazky' — and Raiffeisenbank's own documents use the English 'SNP (Senior Non Preferred)' inside Czech text. Similarly, 'covered bond' has three coexisting Czech renderings depending on vintage and legal basis: the historic 'hypoteční zástavní listy (HZL)', the post-2019 statutory 'kryté dluhopisy' / 'krytý blok', and the EU-label 'evropský krytý dluhopis (prémiový)'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language querying works, but only with an explicitly multi-vintage term set; a single-term query misses whole eras of documents.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any CZ query set for this cell must fire all of {hypoteční zástavní listy, HZL, kryté dluhopisy, krytý blok, evropský krytý dluhopis, emisní dodatek, konečné podmínky, základní prospekt, MREL dluhopisy, způsobilé závazky} plus the English-in-Czech forms (SNP, MREL, HTT, cover pool), or recall collapses.

negative_findings.description: The Czech terms 'dluhopisy' and 'emise dluhopisů' are heavily contaminated by the Czech retail corporate-bond and mini-bond scene (dluhopisy.cz, dluhopisar.cz, srovnavacdluhopisu.cz, KB's large archive of arranged client issues for Accolade, Allwyn, CZG, Dr. Max, RegioJet and others) and by bank product pages selling third-party bonds. Searching 'banka emise dluhopisů' without qualifiers returns mostly non-bank issuers for whom the bank is merely arranger or paying agent.
negative_findings.result_summary: Broad Czech bond queries have low precision for bank-as-issuer material.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design must anchor on issuer-role terms ('emitent', 'povinně uveřejňované informace', 'krytý blok', 'MREL') or on the named six licensed issuers; otherwise the collector fills up with corporate mini-bond noise that belongs to a different cell entirely.

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was consumed before three planned lines of enquiry could be run: (a) the Czech-language route into the ČNB OAM application interface and its filter vocabulary, (b) ČNB ARAD time series for HZL/covered-bond outstanding volumes, and (c) MREL/bond issuance by second-tier Czech deposit-takers and building societies (Air Bank / PPF banka, J&T Banka, Fio banka, Českomoravská stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Trinity Bank).
negative_findings.result_summary: Three known-relevant sub-areas were left unsearched; they are recorded as coverage gaps rather than as absent sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence of these from the candidate list reflects a run constraint, not a finding that the sources do not exist. They should be the first queries in any follow-up run for this cell.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching was run in parallel with Czech throughout ('Czech building society annual report subsidiary Erste KBC Societe Generale Raiffeisen disclosure', 'Czech credit union cooperative savings annual report disclosure Pillar 3') and returned almost nothing usable at entity level for this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: English queries returned parent-group material (KBC Group annual reports, the 2019 KBC/ČSOB buyout of BSH's 45% ČMSS stake) and generic EBA/Basel Pillar 3 documents, but no CZ non-bank subsidiary disclosure pages. Of the five building societies, only Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna (confirmed bilingual PDFs 2020–2025) and MONETA Stavební Spořitelna (bilingual IR pages) publish English. Buřinka's annual-report index is Czech-only; ČNB's disclosure indexes were reached only via Czech URLs. No English-language disclosure page was found for any credit union or pension company.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector built on English queries would miss roughly the entire cell. Retrieval must be Czech-first, and downstream extraction must handle Czech financial terminology (výroční zpráva, účetní závěrka, účastnický fond, transformovaný fond, povinně uveřejňované informace) rather than expecting English equivalents.

negative_findings.description: The URL ČNB's official bank-disclosure index still gives for ČSOB Stavební spořitelna is https://www.cmss.cz/informace-dle-vyhlasky-cnb, from the pre-rebrand Českomoravská stavební spořitelna era.
negative_findings.result_summary: One fetch of that URL returned ECONNREFUSED 193.245.72.249:443. A targeted Czech search recovered a live replacement at csobstavebni.cz with both /vyrocni-zpravy and /informace-dle-vyhlasky-cnb. Recorded as a stale-domain hypothesis, not a dead source — the entity is plainly active.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Even the authoritative regulator index carries lagging URLs after rebrands. A collector must treat an index entry failure as a rename signal and re-resolve the entity by name/IČO rather than marking it dead, or it will silently lose the largest building society in the market.

negative_findings.description: https://www.modrapyramida.cz/dokumenty could not be fetched by the strict-TLS fetcher.
negative_findings.result_summary: Error: 'Hostname/IP does not match certificate's altnames: Host: www.modrapyramida.cz is not in the cert's altnames: DNS:www.kb.cz, DNS:kb.cz'. Hypothesis: the domain is now served from Komerční banka infrastructure as part of the ongoing absorption of Modrá pyramida into KB, so content is live but the certificate does not cover the legacy hostname.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most strategically loaded entity in the cell (branch conversion to KB poradenská místa, advisor absorption, servicing moved to KB+) and it is exactly the one a naive fetcher drops. Collection needs a browser-grade client, plus kb.cz and Sbírka listin as parallel routes.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for Investiční společnost České spořitelny's mandatory disclosures as a candidate bank-group investment firm.
negative_findings.result_summary: ISČS ceased to exist as a Czech legal entity: Erste Asset Management GmbH became sole shareholder in 2009 and a cross-border merger in 2015 absorbed ISČS into Erste Asset Management GmbH, with services now offered through 'Erste Asset Management GmbH, pobočka Česká republika' (IČO 04107128, registered at the Municipal Court in Prague). A branch files differently from a Czech joint-stock company, so there is no equivalent standalone CZ statutory annual report.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: One of the largest bank-group asset managers in CZ has no entity-level Czech annual report to sweep. Coverage of the Erste/ČS asset-management side must instead come from Erste AM group disclosures, REICO (the ČS-group real-estate investment company, which does remain a Czech entity), and AKAT aggregates — otherwise the cell's investment-firm coverage looks complete when it is not.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for the Asociace družstevních záložen (ADZ), the credit-union trade body, expecting an association counterpart to AČSS and APS ČR.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only third-party directory profiles were returned (uspory.cz, penize.cz, fintimes.cz, druzstevni-inkubator.cz). Background surfaced: ADZ founded 2001 by WPB Capital, Prague Credit Union and DZ NOVA; roughly five of the credit unions described as members. No official ADZ domain appeared in results, and no association statistics comparable to AČSS or APS ČR were located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The credit-union segment has no usable association-level aggregator. Sector totals for družstevní záložny must come from ČNB ARAD and the supervision report, and entity detail must be assembled union by union — a materially more expensive collection pattern than for building societies or pension companies.

negative_findings.description: Sought a consolidated, machine-readable source of branch counts, advisor headcount or self-service/ATM estate for the non-bank licensed entities in this cell.
negative_findings.result_summary: No such registry or dataset was found in Czech or English. Channel facts surfaced only as narrative: KB press releases dating the conversion of ~190 Modrá pyramida branches to KB advisory points and the move of ~500 advisors into KB's network, and Patria Finance's own description of developing its trading applications. Nothing equivalent exists as a periodic structured feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core value — entity-level channel and technology signal — must be extracted from prose in annual reports and press releases rather than read off a table. Collection design should assume text extraction plus manual review, and should prioritise the narrative sections of výroční zprávy over the financial statements.

negative_findings.description: Two plausible-looking disclosure URLs returned HTTP 404 on first fetch: https://www.nrb.cz/o-nas/povinne-zverejnovane-informace/ and https://ceb.cz/informace/povinne-zverejnovane-informace1/vz-html (the latter appeared as a search-result title). Both were constructed or copied rather than confirmed from live navigation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Correct live paths were then recovered from each site's own navigation: NRB uses 'povinně UVEŘEJŇOVANÉ informace' (https://www.nrb.cz/o-nas/povinne-uverejnovane-informace/) while ČEB uses 'povinně ZVEŘEJŇOVANÉ informace' (https://www.ceb.cz/informace/povinne-zverejnovane-informace/) with annual reports at /o-bance/vyrocni-zpravy/. Neither 404 is evidence the sites or sections are dead — both are alive under different slugs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Czech institutions use two near-identical statutory phrases (uveřejňované vs. zveřejňované) for the same disclosure duty. A collector that hard-codes one variant will silently miss entities using the other, and a liveness checker will record false deaths.

negative_findings.description: Searched for English-language annual reports of Česká exportní banka. The ČEB annual-report index lists Czech-only PDFs for every year 2012-2025 (filenames end in -cs.pdf or are Czech-titled consolidated auditor reports); no English annual report was listed on that page.
negative_findings.result_summary: An English site section exists at ceb.cz/en/, but no English annual report file was identified for any year.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any downstream comparison of Czech state export finance against peer ECAs or export banks will need Czech-language parsing or machine translation for ČEB; budgeting for that now avoids a silent coverage hole.

negative_findings.description: No English-language version of Garanční systém finančního trhu materials (annual reports, budgets, bond prospectuses) was identified. All documents observed on garancnisystem.cz/dokumenty are Czech-titled.
negative_findings.result_summary: GSFT deposit-insurance and resolution-fund reporting appears to be Czech-only in the material found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deposit-insurance fund size and resolution-fund build-up are core comparative metrics across EU markets; Czech-only publication means cross-country benchmarking of the Czech safety net requires local-language extraction.

negative_findings.description: Looked for machine-readable feeds (RSS/Atom, JSON, open-data endpoints) published by the in-cell institutions themselves — NRB, ČEB, EGAP, GSFT. None were identified during this pass; all content is HTML index pages plus PDFs.
negative_findings.result_summary: No first-party API or feed found for any of the four core state financial institutions. EGAP additionally uses tokenised one-time-looking download URLs (/cs/file/<id>/download?token=...).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be scrape-based with change detection rather than feed-based, and EGAP download links cannot be cached across runs. The only genuinely machine-readable routes in this cell are third-party or cross-cutting (Hlídač státu API, MONITOR státní pokladna open data, Registr smluv dumps).

negative_findings.description: Searched in Czech for EGAP interim/quarterly statistics on insured export volumes ('čtvrtletní data', 'statistiky pojištěného vývozu') as a higher-frequency alternative to the annual report.
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated quarterly statistics page or dataset was located on egap.cz. The recurring public figures (insured volume, profit, number of policies, destination countries, Fond Ukrajina volumes) appear to be released annually via press release and then re-syndicated by ČTK-fed outlets.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Intra-year visibility on Czech state-backed export capacity is limited to press releases and to the semi-annual reporting EGAP makes to the Chamber of Deputies; the parliamentary route (psp.cz) may therefore be the only sub-annual quantitative channel and should be prioritised.

negative_findings.description: For Garanční fond obchodníků s cennými papíry (gfo.cz), search results surfaced the homepage and third-party restatements of the fund's rules and older annual reports (2004, 2007, 2016 referenced) but no annual-report index page on gfo.cz was directly confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Entity and its statutory role are confirmed; the location and completeness of its own annual-report archive are not. This is unverified, not absent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: GFO completes the Czech financial safety-net map alongside GSFT; if its own publication is thin, or.justice.cz filings and CNB records become the fallback route and that needs to be decided before the collection run.

negative_findings.description: Ministry of Finance content is served from two hostnames: legacy mfcr.cz and current mf.gov.cz. A fetch of https://www.mfcr.cz/cs/verejny-sektor/majetek-statu/majetkove-ucasti returned HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect to https://mf.gov.cz/cs/verejny-sektor/majetek-statu/majetkove-ucasti. Both hostnames also appear in live search results with different path prefixes (/cs/kontrola-a-regulace/... vs /cs/verejny-sektor/...).
negative_findings.result_summary: Same content, two hosts and at least two path taxonomies. Not a failure, but a deduplication and link-rot hazard.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without host and path normalisation, the MF ownership register and financial-market reports will be double-counted or lost when legacy redirects are eventually retired.

negative_findings.description: Multiple independent Czech sources (MPO and MF press releases, NKÚ-related coverage) indicate the government decided to integrate Česká exportní banka into Národní rozvojová banka, with ČEB becoming a subsidiary of NRB, supported by a dedicated Act on the National Development Bank passing the Chamber of Deputies in 2024.
negative_findings.result_summary: This is a live restructuring affecting two of the cell's core entities, not a stable steady state. Reporting perimeter, consolidation basis and possibly the publishing domain (ceb.cz) are at risk of change.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Time series built on standalone ČEB reporting may break; consolidated NRB group reporting may absorb ČEB figures. The source map must record entity lineage (ČMZRB -> NRB; ČEB -> NRB subsidiary) or year-on-year comparisons will be silently wrong.

coverage_gaps.description: Two parent-group IR estates relevant to this cell were not located to a confirmed URL: Société Générale (60% owner of Komerční banka, which reports KB inside International Retail Banking) and UniCredit SpA (parent of UniCredit Bank CZ&SK). Both were referenced only indirectly through third-party coverage in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted en and fr/it searches for the SG and UniCredit SpA investor-relations report pages and confirm the exact quarterly-results paths, then add them alongside the Erste and KBC entries. Deliberately not guessed here rather than recorded as invented URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: Česká spořitelna's entire document estate sits behind a client-side SPA at /cs/dokumenty-ke-stazeni with numeric category IDs in the URL fragment. Category IDs were captured for 2022–2026 results sets, results presentations (18) and Debt Investors & MREL (1124), but the full category registry and the backing data endpoint are unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Drive the SPA once with a headless browser to enumerate every category ID and label, and capture the XHR the app issues so future collection can hit the JSON endpoint directly. Persist the ID-to-label registry, since the year categories get a fresh ID annually.

coverage_gaps.description: Earnings-call audio, webcasts and transcripts were confirmed only at parent-group level (Erste publishes audio and video webcasts per quarter). Whether Komerční banka publishes its own conference-call recording or transcript, and where, was not established — the financial calendar page references investor events but the artefact itself was not located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the KB financial calendar and a recent KB results permalink specifically hunting for a webcast/replay link or transcript PDF. Also check whether third-party transcript aggregators are the only route, which would raise a licensing question worth flagging before collection.

coverage_gaps.description: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia is a single legal entity covering both markets and files under both Czech and Slovak law, but this run's language scope is cs and en only. Slovak-language disclosure surfaces on unicreditbank.sk were seen in passing (annual report PDFs under /content/dam/cee2020-pws-sk/) and not pursued. The same applies to ČSOB's Slovak arm following the 365.bank combination.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Either extend language scope to sk for these two issuers specifically, or record explicitly that CZ-attributable figures for UniCredit Bank CZ&SK must be derived from segment notes rather than headline entity figures — otherwise the Slovak balance sheet will silently contaminate CZ market sizing.

coverage_gaps.description: ESEF/XBRL machine-readable filings were confirmed only for Komerční banka, from 2020 onward. Whether ČS, ČSOB or UniCredit Bank CZ&SK publish ESEF packages — and if so where — is unknown, since ESEF obligation attaches to issuers with securities on a regulated market, which all four have via debt even where equity is unlisted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check each issuer's mandatory-disclosure page for an ESEF or XBRL package alongside the PDF annual report. If absent locally, check whether the Prague Stock Exchange or CNB central storage holds the filings, which would give a single structured-format entry point for the whole cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Two obvious pointer estates were repeatedly implied by evidence but not scouted, as they sit outside this cell: the Prague Stock Exchange / PSE issuer disclosure pages and the Czech National Bank's central storage of regulated information, which is the statutory repository the kurzy.cz and patria.cz mirrors appear to draw from.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm another scout owns the PSE and CNB central-storage cell. If nobody does, they should be added — a single regulated-information repository would de-risk the csob.cz and unicreditbank.cz bot-defence problems for the whole cell at once.

coverage_gaps.description: Air Bank a.s. is one of the most strategically interesting challengers in the cell — PPF-owned, a repeated first mover on retail UX and pricing — yet this pass located only its consolidated annual report PDFs and its press room. No Air Bank quarterly ČNB/ČBA disclosure annex and no capital-adequacy filing was found, and the regulator-designated disclosure page does not link them. Its half-year position is visible only through PPF's 'Air Bank Group' combined results releases, which are unaudited and use a group perimeter that differs from the bank's own.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a targeted follow-up specifically for Air Bank quarterly disclosures using Czech regulatory vocabulary ('povinně uveřejňované informace k 30.6.', 'kapitálová přiměřenost', 'příloha 1'), probe /file-download/ for annex-style filenames, and fall back to the Sbírka listin filing for Air Bank a.s. (resolve its IČO via ARES first). Confirm whether the PPF 'Air Bank Group' perimeter includes Home Credit CZ/SK before using those numbers as bank figures.

coverage_gaps.description: Two of the ten actors named in this coverage cell are no longer live banks: Max banka merged into Banka CREDITAS and Hello bank wound down its Czech operations. That leaves eight live actors, of which one (mBank) has no Czech statutory disclosure at all. The cell rationale's premise — a long tail of licensed banks each carrying full statutory annual-report duties — holds for only six of the ten named entities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reissue the cell roster as: MONETA, Raiffeisenbank a.s., Air Bank, Fio banka, Banka CREDITAS (now including the Max product line), Trinity Bank, Partners Banka as Czech-licensed banks with full duties, plus mBank CZ as a single-licence branch requiring parent-group collection. Backfill the vacated slots from the ČNB disclosure-link list, which names roughly two dozen banks and therefore contains second-tier institutions not currently assigned to any cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Fetching the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links established that it covers roughly two dozen banks, materially more than the ten named in this cell plus the big four handled elsewhere. This pass did not enumerate and classify the remainder, so an unknown number of second-tier and specialist Czech-licensed banks (including building societies and specialist mortgage or corporate banks) currently have no scout assigned.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do a mechanical full extraction of the ČNB list into a bank-to-disclosure-URL table, diff it against the union of all coverage cells in this run, and assign the residual banks to a follow-up cell. This is cheap, deterministic and closes the universe-boundary question for workstream A1 in a single pass.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell rationale specifically justifies a separate scout on the grounds that these banks disclose branch, ATM and digital-channel decisions that systemic banks bury. This pass found the channels where such news appears (each bank's press room, and Air Bank / Partners Banka releases that quantified mobile-app usage and client milestones) but did not locate any structured, comparable branch-count or ATM-network dataset per bank. ČNB ARAD and the payment-system statistics were identified as the likely home for aggregate channel data, but the specific series were not confirmed in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated follow-up on channel-footprint sources: identify the exact ARAD series ids for branch and payment-infrastructure counts, check whether ČNB supervisory statistics publish per-institution branch numbers, and evaluate ATM-network operators and the interbank ATM landscape as a separate source family. Also test whether each bank's annual report contains a consistent branch/ATM disclosure that could be extracted into a comparable series.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage was achieved for every live actor: Czech-language queries were the ones that surfaced the ČNB disclosure-link list, the Fio quarterly XLSX annexes, the Trinity Bank archive, the Partners Banka document hub, the Max banka merger evidence, the Hello bank exit and the mBank Czech press portal — none of which reliably surfaced in English. The reverse gap is real though: English-language disclosure in this cell is thin and uneven. MONETA and Trinity Bank (2020 onward) publish English annual reports, Raiffeisenbank maintains an /en/ tree and an English investor presentation, and Partners Banka publishes English annual reports; Air Bank, Fio banka and Banka CREDITAS were not observed publishing English editions of their statutory reports in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Czech as the mandatory primary collection language for this cell and English as an opportunistic parallel. For downstream analysis, budget for machine translation of Czech statutory PDFs rather than assuming English editions exist, and verify per-bank whether an English edition is a true translation or an abridged summary before treating the two as interchangeable.

coverage_gaps.description: Pointer and regulator-side sources were covered well (ČNB disclosure-link list, JERRS with its web services and open data, the Central Repository of Regulated Information, Sbírka listin, the national open-data catalogue). Independent third-party assessment sources were not: no credit-rating agency coverage of these banks was pulled beyond noting that MONETA maintains a ratings page, no auditor-identity mapping was compiled, and no ČNB supervisory enforcement or sanction record was searched. Job postings, procurement records and vendor case studies — which reveal payments and core-banking technology decisions indirectly — were not explored at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up pass on assessment and reveals-indirectly source families: rating-agency issuer pages for MONETA, Raiffeisenbank and Banka CREDITAS (a bond issuer); ČNB enforcement and sanction decisions; auditor identity per bank from the annual reports; and technology-vendor press releases, careers pages and public procurement mentions as indirect indicators of payments-platform investment.

coverage_gaps.description: Sources found in this pass disagreed on the timing of the Max banka absorption into Banka CREDITAS — press coverage placed the completed legal merger at 1 October 2024 with a transitional dual bank-code period, while CREDITAS's own 2025 results narrative described completing the Max banka integration during 2025. The maxbanka.eu archive is consistent with the earlier date (documents stop at FY2023 and Q3 2024) but does not state a merger date. Banka CREDITAS's acquisition of the Maltese MeDirect group was also identified as a major perimeter change affecting comparability, but its effective date and accounting treatment were not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve both dates from primary records rather than press: pull the merger deed and the relevant annual report from Banka CREDITAS's Sbírka listin file, and check the ČNB JERRS as-of-date search to see when Max banka a.s. disappeared from the licensed-bank list. Flag FY2024 and FY2025 CREDITAS figures as perimeter-inconsistent until the MeDirect consolidation date is confirmed.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank acquiring arms other than Komerční banka (KB SmartPay) and ČSOB (platbakartou.csob.cz) were not individually mapped to a source. Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit Bank, MONETA Money Bank, Fio banka and Air Bank all touch card acceptance or issuing-side processing in Czechia, and several appeared only incidentally (a UniCredit product-terms PDF, a Fio terminal page) rather than as tracked sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one pass per bank in Czech using the pattern '<bank> akceptace platebních karet' plus '<bank> tiskové centrum / pro média', resolve each bank's acquiring subsidiary or partner in ARES, and record both the press channel and the merchant terms-and-conditions PDF path. Establishing which bank uses which processor is the specific output to aim for.

coverage_gaps.description: Issuer processing and card-platform outsourcing — arguably the cell's most strategically important signal — has no dedicated source. No Czech-language term for 'issuer processing' surfaced in any search; Czech practice appears to use the English phrase or to describe it periphrastically ('zpracování karetních transakcí pro vydavatele', 'zpracovatelské centrum').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat this as a glossary gap first: harvest the actual Czech phrasing from CardMag back issues and from Global Payments Europe / Nexi CZ statutory annual reports (where the scope of business is described in Czech), then rebuild queries from the harvested wording. Contract-level evidence will more likely come from the Registr smluv and NEN than from any newsroom.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's Czech-language coverage is solid for acquiring/merchant-facing terms but thin for processing/technical vocabulary, and there is no Slovak-language coverage even though several of these entities (Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi) run Czech and Slovak operations from shared Prague or Bratislava infrastructure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the glossary with harvested processing terminology (see above) and add a small Slovak query set ('akceptácia platobných kariet', 'spracovanie kartových transakcií') plus the Slovak business register, since CZ/SK announcements are frequently issued jointly and the Slovak side sometimes discloses what the Czech side does not.

coverage_gaps.description: No source was found that reveals acquiring market share or portfolio switches indirectly through third-party observation — for example merchant-side gateway/terminal technology detection across Czech e-shops, scheme (Visa/Mastercard) licensee or principal-member lists for Czechia, or PCI DSS validated-provider listings scoped to Czech entities. The 'reveals-indirectly' category is therefore under-served relative to the direct and pointer categories.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate the Czech PCI resource pcistandard.cz linked from the SBK site, the card schemes' published lists of licensed acquirers/principal members for the Czech market, and technology-detection datasets over the .cz e-commerce long tail as proxies for gateway and acquirer share. Each would give an independent read that does not depend on any actor choosing to disclose.

coverage_gaps.description: Because the WebSearch quota was exhausted before this cell began, all discovery ran through single-page Seznam.cz HTML results, direct URL probing and the ARES API. No pagination beyond the first result page was possible and no second search engine was usable (DuckDuckGo served CAPTCHAs, Mojeek returned 403).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available, prioritising second- and third-page results for the six seed queries and adding the corrected Czech terminology. Expect the long tail — smaller PSPs, ISOs, softPOS entrants, bank-internal processing units — to be where the additions are, since the head of the market is well covered by this slice.

coverage_gaps.description: Sbírka listin entry points were resolved and their subjektId values confirmed for seven entities, but the individual filing documents inside each collection were not enumerated, so the recency and completeness of each company's filings is unknown. Czech entities not infrequently file late or incompletely.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each tracked IČO, enumerate the deeds listing and record the most recent accounting period actually filed, so analysis distinguishes 'no disclosure' from 'disclosure not yet due' and flags chronic late filers.

coverage_gaps.description: No search-engine discovery was possible in this run (WebSearch budget exhausted before the first query). Coverage rests entirely on first-principles URL hypothesis and snowballing, which cannot find actors that no fetched page links to.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with WebSearch budget available, issuing the six seed queries plus the extended cs query set: 'seznam platebních institucí ČNB', 'instituce elektronických peněz Česká republika seznam', 'platební brána pro e-shop srovnání 2026', 'poskytovatel platebních služeb malého rozsahu registrace', 'objem transakcí platební brána Česko miliard korun', 'okamžité platby e-shop platební brána'.

coverage_gaps.description: The seed list omitted GP webpay (Global payments Europe, s.r.o.), which self-describes as the most-used payment gateway in Czech e-shops — found only by snowballing. If the single largest actor was missing from the seeds, other significant actors are probably missing too. Actors identified but NOT yet source-profiled in this pass: Shoptet Pay (launched 2021-09-01 per Lupa.cz), Worldline CZ as a direct entity, Barion, Pays.cz, Fondy, and the meal-voucher/benefit e-money issuers (Pluxee/Sodexo, Edenred, Up Česká republika, Benefit Plus) which are licensed instituce elektronických peněz in scope for the 'e-money institutions' half of this cell but were not investigated at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Rebuild the actor map from the authoritative bottom up: pull the full platební instituce and instituce elektronických peněz role lists from JERRS/WS JERRS, cross-reference against the APEK seznam členů, and profile every entity that appears in either but not in this slice. Explicitly cover the e-money/benefit-card segment, which is currently at zero coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Instant-payment (okamžité platby) adoption — an explicitly stated goal of this cell — was not evidenced in ANY source inspected. No gateway published instant-payment volume, share or adoption data. Similarly, payment-method mix (card vs bank transfer vs wallet vs BNPL) was absent from every corporate source, including the two most likely candidates (Comgate blog, Shoptet press).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do not rely on the gateway layer for these two metrics. Route them to ČNB payment statistics and to APEK's studie/data programme (data.apek.cz), and check whether ČSOB/ČS/KB or the CNB's platební styk statistics publish okamžité platby series. Re-scope this cell's expected output to merchant wins, product/rail roadmap, ownership changes and company-level volume claims.

coverage_gaps.description: Three sources need collection machinery this slice did not establish: Revolut's newsroom (HTTP 403, needs headless browser), Worldline IR (JS-rendered, near-empty response to plain fetch), and WS JERRS (requires a commercial certificate from eIdentity/I.CA/PostSignum plus an electronically signed request to jerrsws@cnb.cz).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision a headless-browser collector tier for bot-defended and JS-rendered sources. Separately, start the ČNB WS JERRS certificate procurement now — it has an administrative lead time and gates the single most authoritative actor-map feed for this cell. Test the JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ p_seznam enumeration first, as it may make the certificate unnecessary.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage was achieved for the domestic layer — cs terms (platební brána, tisková zpráva, pro média, výroční zpráva, účetní závěrka, obchodní rejstřík, sbírka listin, platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, odložená platba, objem transakcí, zprávy a média, pro novináře) were used throughout and drove most successful discoveries. However, Slovak-language coverage was NOT attempted despite being materially relevant: Besteron is NBS-licensed and passporting into CZ, and GoPay reports CZ+SK merchant counts jointly. Nothing was collected in sk.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a Slovak term set (platobná brána, tlačová správa, výročná správa, platobná inštitúcia, inštitúcia elektronických peňazí, Národná banka Slovenska) and cover the NBS register plus the SK-language variants of Besteron and GoPay, since SK-licensed entities serving CZ merchants are otherwise invisible to a cs-only sweep.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one CZ trade-press pointer (Lupa.cz's 'Platební brány' tag, 22 articles) was profiled, and it proved highly productive — it independently dated the GoPay/Worldline ownership completion and surfaced Shoptet Pay. No other Czech outlet was inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Profile parallel CZ outlets and their payments/fintech topic tags: e15.cz, CzechCrunch, Měšec.cz, Podnikatel.cz, Hospodářské noviny, Forbes CZ, and the specialist banking press. Prefer topic-tag and RSS endpoints over homepage scraping, and store headline+date+URL metadata only, given editorial content is copyrighted.

coverage_gaps.description: Several assertions in this slice are hypotheses carried forward rather than confirmed facts: dataor.justice.cz contents and formats (named in portal text, never fetched); whether or.justice.cz Sbírka listin documents are free PDFs (not confirmed on the landing page); whether Adyen's shareholder letters contain an EMEA/Europe volume breakout (not confirmed on the IR landing page); the exact filenames of GoPay's ucetni-zaverky-*.pdf files (a placeholder pattern was reported, deliberately not guessed); Comgate's 'Zmínili se o nás' correct slug; whether Adyen has a Prague office among its 28 cities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve each of these with a targeted fetch in the next pass before any collector is built on top of them. None should be treated as established. In particular, confirm Sbírka listin document access is free before scoping the statutory-filings pipeline, since that pipeline is the backbone of annual-report coverage for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: The mandatory bilingual search-engine sweep was not performed at all because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this cell started. Prepared but unexecuted Czech queries included: 'Twisto tisková zpráva odložená platba obchodníci výsledky'; 'Skip Pay ČSOB odložená platba tisková zpráva integrace'; 'nákup na splátky online platba později Česko tisková zpráva integrace'; 'poskytovatel spotřebitelských úvěrů Česká republika hospodářské výsledky výroční zpráva'; 'kup teď zaplať později Česko podíl na trhu'; 'PlatímPak Raiffeisenbank odložená platba e-shopy'. Prepared English queries included: 'Czech BNPL buy now pay later press release merchant integration results'; 'Home Credit Group annual report Czech Republic consumer finance'; 'Czech Republic deferred payment provider market share 2026'.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available, executing the query list above in both cs and en, and going past the first page of results. Treat the present candidate list as a verified seed set to be extended, not replaced.

coverage_gaps.description: The long tail of Czech consumer-credit providers was identified by name but not individually profiled: Zaplo Finance s.r.o. (ČLFA member), PROFI CREDIT Czech a.s., Creditstar Czech s.r.o., CreditPortal a.s., AvaFin Czech s.r.o., Simfina a.s. (all SOLUS members), plus Provident Financial CZ and Fair Credit. ČLFA states it has 14 licensed consumer-credit providers as members, so at least a handful remain unnamed here.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve the full ČNB JERRS list of nebankovní poskytovatelé spotřebitelského úvěru into a canonical actor table keyed by IČO, then profile each for a press channel and a Sbírka listin filing history. The JERRS web service makes this cheap and systematic.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign BNPL entrants into the Czech market were not investigated. Klarna, PayPo and similar pan-European providers were neither confirmed nor ruled out as active in Czech checkouts. Notably, none of them appeared in the Shoptet payments addon catalogue, which is suggestive of limited Czech platform penetration but is not proof of absence.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check the addon catalogues of the other Czech e-shop platforms (Upgates, FastCentrik, Retailys, eBrana were all named by Skip Pay as integration targets) and the major gateways' method lists for foreign BNPL brands, then follow any hit back to the provider's Czech-language pages.

coverage_gaps.description: The 'wallet providers' half of the cell brief is materially under-covered. Twisto and Skip Pay were treated primarily as BNPL, and no dedicated pass was made on Czech wallet or stored-value propositions — Revolut CZ, Fidoo, Qerko and any bank-issued wallet arms were not examined, and the boundary against the card-acceptance cell was not tested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated wallet sub-pass using Czech terms 'digitální peněženka', 'elektronická peněženka', 'platební karta v mobilu', 'předplacená karta', cross-referenced against the ČNB list of instituce elektronických peněz in JERRS, and agree an explicit boundary with the neighbouring cells.

coverage_gaps.description: Regulatory enforcement and supervisory output was not collected. ČNB sanction decisions, supervisory benchmark reports, the Zpráva o výkonu dohledu and the Zpráva o finanční stabilitě were all reasoned about as relevant categories but none were fetched; likewise, no court or arbitration records, no ombudsman (finanční arbitr) decisions, and no Česká obchodní inspekce consumer-protection actions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a supervisory/enforcement sub-pass covering cnb.cz sanction lists and supervision reports, the Finanční arbitr's decision database, and ČOI. Enforcement documents are high-credibility, dated, and often the only public source of adverse detail about consumer-credit conduct.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech specialist personal-finance and retail-trade media were not fetched on this pass — Peníze.cz, Měšec.cz, Finparáda, Lupa.cz, e15, Hospodářské noviny, MediaGuru and retail titles are all plausible carriers of BNPL pricing comparisons and merchant-adoption reporting. Only CzechCrunch was reached.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch and classify each of the above, prioritising those that publish structured product comparisons (Finparáda, Měšec.cz) since those double as pricing datasets. Cashbot's /napsali-o-nas/ press-clipping page is a cheap way to discover which outlets actually cover this sector.

coverage_gaps.description: No specific ARAD dataset covering consumer credit or non-bank credit providers was identified, because the ARAD entry point returned an empty JS shell. The sector-level quantitative series that would let provider claims be benchmarked therefore remains unlocated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Access ARAD with a headless browser or via its documented data-export interface, identify the series codes for spotřebitelské úvěry (bank and non-bank), and register those codes in the collection plan alongside the ČLFA statistics.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-duopoly card schemes operating in the Czech market were not scouted: American Express (americanexpress.com/czech, americanexpress.cz), Diners Club, JCB and Discover all appear as live links from the SBK/CardMag industry pages, indicating a CZ presence, but none was fetched or classified in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe each scheme's Czech-market presence and press channel, and check whether SBK's statistics break out non-Visa/Mastercard volumes. Start from the SBK homepage link block, which already lists all four.

coverage_gaps.description: Interchange-fee and scheme-fee disclosure pages for the Czech market — which the schemes are obliged to publish under the EU Interchange Fee Regulation — were not located. Two candidate paths were tried: visa.cz/about-visa/interchange.html and /o-spolecnosti-visa/interchange.html (both 404), and mastercard.cz/cs-cz/podnikatele/podpora/mezibankovni-poplatky.html (403).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the current IFR disclosure URLs for Visa CZ and Mastercard CZ via on-site navigation (headless browser) rather than path guessing. These pages are the only public, quantitative, scheme-published pricing data for the CZ market.

coverage_gaps.description: Wallet and tokenisation operators sitting on top of the card rails in CZ — Apple Pay, Google Pay/Google Wallet, Garmin/Fitbit Pay, and the schemes' Click to Pay deployment (a Click to Pay page exists at visa.cz/business/consumers/click-to-pay.html) — were not scouted as sources. They are neither banks nor vendors, so like the schemes they risk falling between cells.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide explicitly whether wallet operators belong to this infrastructure cell or to a vendor cell, then scout their CZ-facing announcement channels. Tokenisation share is a headline metric in Visa CZ releases, so the two are already entangled.

coverage_gaps.description: This slice is heavily weighted to direct operator sources (ČNB, Visa, Mastercard, Bank iD) plus a small number of indirect/pointer sources. Aggregator and archive classes are thin: no news-aggregation feed, no RSS inventory, and no web-archive strategy was established for the schemes' press pages despite the demonstrated risk that scheme sites are bot-defended and that mirrors carry broken links.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a Wayback/archive.org capture strategy for visa.cz and mastercard.cz newsrooms, and inventory RSS/Atom feeds across all candidates (none was confirmed in this pass) so polling can move from HTML diffing to feeds where available.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech-language coverage is strong for ČNB, Visa CZ, Bank iD, SBK and CardMag. It is absent for the SEPA/EU layer, and no Slovak- or German-language comparator was scouted even though zbk.sk (the Slovak bank card association, the direct analogue of SBK) is linked from the SBK homepage and would provide a near-identical dataset for cross-border benchmarking.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: If cross-border comparison is in scope for later workstreams, scout zbk.sk as the Slovak mirror of SBK. Within CZ scope, hunt specifically for a Czech-language SEPA/instant-payment scheme description outside ČNB (likely ČBA-hosted).

coverage_gaps.description: Three of the highest-value targets in this cell (mastercard.cz, the EPC document library and register of participants, and the ČNB ARAD database) are all unreachable by plain HTTP fetching — two via 403 bot defence, one via a JavaScript SPA. No headless-browser collection capability was exercised or confirmed available during this scout.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a headless-browser collector with a realistic fingerprint before the collection phase for this cell, and validate it against exactly these three targets. Without it, roughly a third of the cell's critical/high-priority sources cannot be ingested and would be misrecorded as dead.

coverage_gaps.description: Because zero keyword searches could be run, discovery was confined to what could be reached by domain guessing and link-following from a small seed set. Entire plausible source types for this cell were therefore never tested: Czech payments trade newsletters, LinkedIn/X accounts of the schemes' CZ country managers (SBK's own X account @SdruzeniK was seen but not assessed), scheme-sponsored CZ consumer research reports, and tender/procurement notices for national payment infrastructure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with the WebSearch budget restored, executing the assigned cs and en seed queries plus snowballed terms, and treat the present slice as a verified core rather than a complete map.

coverage_gaps.description: There is no public source that splits the Czech ATM estate by owner/operator. ČNB reports only ATMs operated by Czech banks (4.9 thousand at end-2025); Euronet self-reports ~10% of a ~5,000 machine national total; SBK's whole-estate series stopped around 2011. The three cannot be reconciled without an operator-attributed dataset.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a derived fleet-attribution estimate: take the ČNB bank-operated series as the denominator anchor, add an OpenStreetMap amenity=atm extract with operator tags for operator mix, sample banky.cz/Mapy.com listings for corroboration, and reconcile annually against Euronet Services' Sbírka listin filing. Document the estimate's method and error bars explicitly rather than quoting Euronet's share claim as fact.

coverage_gaps.description: The core financial disclosures for every Czech actor in this cell (Euronet Services 25608452, Loomis Czech Republic 26110709, Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) 27590151, Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) 08829969) exist only as PDFs inside the court Sbírka listin — often scanned — and were not retrieved in this run. Chytrý rejstřík indicates 56 documents on file for Euronet Services alone.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a Sbírka listin harvesting pipeline: resolve IČO via ARES, enumerate document rows per company and year, download účetní závěrka / výroční zpráva / zpráva auditora PDFs, OCR scanned filings, and extract revenue, EBIT, headcount, related-party balances and any narrative mention of bankomaty/síť/outsourcing. Backfill at least five years to establish trend.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the large, internationally-owned CIT operators were identified (Loomis, Brink's, plus the unresolved G4S question, and ČP Security surfaced incidentally as a money-transport provider). Smaller and regional Czech cash-transport and cash-processing firms were not enumerated, and no association directory covers them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a systematic ARES sweep by CZ-NACE (security activities and auxiliary financial-service codes) combined with keyword matching on business-activity descriptions ('převoz cenin', 'přeprava a zpracování hotovosti'), then cross-check against KPKB ČR member directories and procurement award notices to build a full Czech cash-logistics actor list with IČOs.

coverage_gaps.description: Discovery in this slice ran on a single engine (Seznam.cz), first page only, because the WebSearch budget was exhausted and DuckDuckGo/Mojeek were blocked. English-language and international-trade-press coverage of the Czech ATM/CIT market is therefore thin in this slice, and no result set was paged beyond the first ten hits.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell's query set on Google/Bing with a raised WebSearch budget, going at least three result pages deep, and add English-language queries targeting international cash-industry sources (ATM industry associations, CEE payments trade press, ATM/cash-handling market reports) plus site-scoped queries against euronetatms.cz, brinks.cz and cz.loomis.com for content not surfaced by Seznam.

coverage_gaps.description: Four high-value endpoints were not successfully retrieved — Euronet Worldwide IR, Brink's IR, SEC EDGAR (403), and the smlouvy.gov.cz search UI (timeout) — so parent-level segment disclosure and contract-level evidence remain unread for this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retry with a compliant declared User-Agent and extended timeout; prefer machine interfaces over web UIs — SEC submissions/full-text-search APIs for EEFT and BCO, and the Registr smluv open-data dump filtered by supplier IČO — rather than repeatedly fetching the HTML front ends.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-to-deployer ATM outsourcing and network-participation agreements — the variable that determines how much of the nominally bank-operated Czech fleet is actually run by a third party — are undisclosed by both banks and Euronet. Similarly, bank–CIT cash-logistics contracts are private and outside the public contracts register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Attack indirectly and triangulate: mine Sbírka listin annual-report narratives and related-party notes for both sides; monitor Věstník veřejných zakázek, NEN and Registr smluv for any public-sector or state-controlled counterpart contracts as pricing benchmarks; track bank newsroom announcements for network participation; and consider a structured field-observation protocol recording operator branding and surcharge screens on sampled machines.

coverage_gaps.description: No long-run Czech time series for the deployer-operated ATM estate or for CIT market size was assembled. ČNB's series covers bank-operated machines from 2021 onward in the commentary text, SBK's whole-estate series ends around 2011, and CardMag's archive is unindexed PDF.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reconstruct a joined series by harvesting the ARAD payment-statistics tables for the full available history, back-casting the pre-2012 whole-estate figures from SBK, and text-mining the CardMag PDF archive for interim-year fleet and operator references; document the splice points.

coverage_gaps.description: Mandatory Czech-language (and English) search was not performed at all because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before the cell started. Every seed query and every planned extension query went unrun; discovery relied entirely on fetching known domains, following redirects and enumerating sitemaps.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available (raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION or allocate the cell its own session). Execute the six seed queries plus Czech extensions such as 'implementace jadroveho bankovniho systemu banka CR dodavatel', 'referencni zakaznik banka IT integrator Ceska republika', 'migrace core banking system tiskova zprava', 'dodavatel platebnich systemu banka reference', and site-scoped queries against systemonline.cz and bankovnictvionline.cz.

coverage_gaps.description: Two of the ten named seed actors remain uncharacterised or structurally silent: GEM System (redirect loop on all four URL variants attempted) and Unicorn (JS-rendered; sitemap shows no reference or investor section). Asseco Central Europe, the most important actor in the cell, is 403-blocked.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Deploy a headless browser (Playwright) with a cookie jar, Accept-Language: cs and a realistic user agent for gemsystem.cz, unicorn.com and ce.asseco.com. For Asseco also probe /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml, which WAFs usually leave reachable, to recover the newsroom paths before crawling.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's ten seed vendors are almost certainly not the full Czech bank-technology supplier population. No systematic expansion was performed, and one seed actor (CCA Group) turned out to have no banking references at all — evidence the list was assembled by reputation rather than from a register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest https://www.ictu.cz/clenove-ictu (approx. 60 members) and https://www.systemonline.cz/dodavatele-it-sluzeb-a-reseni/ as the two authoritative vendor registers, then intersect with supplier names appearing in Registr smluv and NEN against financial-sector counterparties. Promote any vendor with a banking reference into per-vendor newsroom monitoring, and demote CCA Group to keyword-triggered monitoring only.

coverage_gaps.description: No demand-side public-buyer channel for state-controlled Czech financial institutions was successfully captured. The CNB procurement page 404'd on the path attempted, and no profil zadavatele was located for Ceska exportni banka (CEB) or Narodni rozvojova banka (NRB, formerly CMZRB) — even though the ICZ CEBIS reference proves CEB buys bespoke banking systems.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the profil zadavatele for CNB, CEB and NRB via the Vestnik verejnych zakazek and NEN rather than by guessing site paths, then add each as a standing source. Cross-reference every awarded supplier against the vendor actor map to convert vendor marketing claims into valued, dated contracts.
