coverage_gaps.description: Non-web vendor disclosure channels were not examined at all: vendor LinkedIn company pages (where Czech integrators often announce bank wins before or instead of a press release), conference programmes and recorded talks (e.g. banking-IT conferences where bank CIOs present their vendor stack), vendor YouTube channels, and job postings that name the specific core-banking or payment platform a vendor is staffing for a named bank.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add LinkedIn company-page monitoring for the seed vendors, and treat Czech IT job boards (jobs.cz, and vendor career sites such as icz.jobs.cz and jsmeprofinit.eu) as a leading indicator: required-skills fields frequently disclose the bank platform in flight months ahead of any case study.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor financial disclosure was identified as a channel (Sbirka listin, KKCG investor pages) but no actual filing was retrieved, and no vendor was resolved to an ICO in this slice. PDF availability and any open-data/API route for or.justice.cz were not confirmed on the search page.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve each of the ten seed vendors to an ICO via ARES, pull the Sbirka listin document list per entity, and confirm whether PDFs are directly addressable or require session-bound navigation. Evaluate the redesigned register at https://verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz/ as the longer-term collection target, and confirm CZ-entity filing status for the Avenga/Cleverlance and Adastra Czech legal entities specifically.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage is uneven across the cell in a way that defeats a single monitoring rule. Monet+, ICZ and CCA publish primarily in Czech; Aricoma, Adastra and Unicorn maintain true CS/EN mirrors (/cs/tiskove-zpravy, /cs/success-stories/, /cs/); Trask and Profinit publish in English only despite being Czech companies; Asseco's language structure is unknown because the site is blocked.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Maintain per-source language profiles rather than one cell-wide keyword set. Run bilingual entity aliases for every bank (e.g. Ceska sporitelna / Czech Savings Bank / CS, Komercni banka / KB, Ceskoslovenska obchodni banka / CSOB, Ceska exportni banka / CEB, Narodni rozvojova banka / NRB) and prefer the /cs/ variant for extraction where a mirror exists, since Czech texts observed carried richer client detail and named executives.

coverage_gaps.description: Zero search-engine queries were executed for this cell (WebSearch budget pre-exhausted; DuckDuckGo CAPTCHA, Mojeek 403, Bing RSS cache-collided). Every candidate here was reached by domain reasoning, direct navigation or on-site search, so the long tail of vendors and the entire class of 'sources I did not already know to guess' is unexplored.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run cell #17 with a restored search budget and execute all six assigned seed queries plus the cs variants verbatim, then diff the resulting candidate set against this slice to measure what domain-reasoning alone missed.

coverage_gaps.description: Named-but-unreached in this pass: Fiserv (timeout), Finastra (403), Printec (403), Thales Group corporate (empty body), Euronet (path migrated). Reasoned-about but never fetched at all: ACI Worldwide (aciworldwide.com/news-and-events 301s to investor.aciworldwide.com/events-and-presentations; the news-releases path then timed out), Worldline (two path guesses 404'd), NCR Voyix, Nexi, Backbase, Mambu, Thought Machine, Sopra Banking Software, Tietoevry, Hyosung TCS, GRGBanking, KAL ATM Software, Cennox, IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient, BS/2 (Penki kontinentai), Asseco SEE.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second pass dedicated to resolving canonical newsroom/IR paths for this list, using a headless browser and following redirect chains rather than guessing paths. Prioritise ACI Worldwide, Worldline, BS/2 and Hyosung as the most CEE-plausible of the unreached set.

coverage_gaps.description: The earnings-call TRANSCRIPT channel — explicitly named in this cell's rationale as where vendors mention country deployments — has no source assigned. IR pages give decks and webcast links, but searchable transcript text (where a CFO says 'Czech Republic' in Q&A) sits with third parties: Motley Fool, Seeking Alpha, Quartr, AlphaSense, Koyfin, and the vendors' own webcast providers. None was evaluated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Evaluate transcript providers for licence terms and machine access, and decide between (a) licensed transcript feeds, (b) speech-to-text over the vendors' own public webcast audio, which avoids third-party copyright entirely, or (c) manual review of the four or five most CZ-relevant issuers' quarterly calls. Option (b) is the cleanest legally.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor LinkedIn newsrooms and regional/country LinkedIn pages are unassessed. For this cell they matter disproportionately: CEE country organisations and local sales teams frequently post a Czech customer win on LinkedIn that never reaches the global newsroom, and LinkedIn is the practical fallback for the vendors whose own sites are WAF-blocked (Finastra, Printec). Vendor LinkedIn URLs were observed on Diebold Nixdorf, Temenos, Comarch, Bankovnictví and Protext pages but none was evaluated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess LinkedIn company-page monitoring for the cell's vendor list under LinkedIn's terms of service; if automated collection is not permissible, define a manual monthly review of the 8-10 most CZ-relevant vendor pages plus their Czech/CEE country pages.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech-language coverage rests on exactly three verified portals (Protext, Bankovnictví online, SystemOnLine) and no cs-language keyword search was ever executed against any index. Nine constructed Czech terms remain unexercised: platební terminál, jádrový bankovní systém, samoobslužná zóna, recyklace hotovosti, výroční zpráva, případová studie, nasazení, implementace, dodavatel.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: With a restored search budget, run each unexercised cs term against a search engine AND against the Protext /vyhledavani/ endpoint, paired with each global vendor name, and add whatever new Czech-language channels surface. Also probe for Czech-language aggregators of foreign corporate news that were not reachable in this pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Only three machine-friendly feeds were confirmed across the entire cell: NCR Atleos IR RSS, Auriga /en/feed/, and ATM Marketplace /rss/. Global Payments IR advertises an RSS feed. Everything else is JS-rendered (Diebold Nixdorf IR), WAF-gated, or offers no feed at all (FIS media room showed none).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision the collector with a headless-browser tier and a compliant declaring User-Agent for SEC before this cell goes live; otherwise budget for HTML-diff scraping on Temenos, FIS, NCR Atleos corporate, Diebold Nixdorf and the Czech portals, and treat the four known feeds as the only low-cost paths.

coverage_gaps.description: The NCR Atleos investor archive (RSS plus numeric /detail/<id>/ URLs) is exposed to the pending Brink's acquisition, and the Euronet news path has already migrated in a way that broke its own redirect (301 to a 404). No snapshotting has been done for either.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mirror the full investor.ncratleos.com press-release archive immediately, before transaction close, and register a successor watch on Brink's investor relations. Re-resolve Euronet's live IR path and prefer EDGAR-by-CIK collection for Euronet so the source survives further site migrations.

coverage_gaps.description: Zero search-engine queries were executable in this cell because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before the first call. Discovery relied entirely on domain guessing plus link-graph snowballing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with WebSearch budget available, using the seeded Czech queries plus snowball-derived terms now known: 'Asociace factoringových společností ČR', 'AČSS stavební spořitelny členové', 'ČASF finančně poradenský trh', 'ČEFTAS ročenka', 'asociace poskytovatelů platebních služeb ČR', 'kryptoměnová asociace ČR'. Specifically hunt for associations with no inbound link from the six seeded bodies.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language mirrors were identified but not systematically enumerated or compared against their Czech originals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Sweep the confirmed English endpoints — cbaonline.cz/about-us/members, cbamonitor.cz/en, apek.cz/en, czechfintech.cz/en/, clfa.cz/o-nas/annual-report and the ČLFA 'Quarterly and yearly results...' statistics page — and diff them against the Czech versions. Czech association sites routinely publish less in English and with a lag, so establish per-source whether the English mirror is complete, partial or stale before any English-only collection is configured.

coverage_gaps.description: Member-only tiers were identified at three associations but their contents remain uncharacterised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Document what sits behind SBK's data.bankovnikarty.cz/secure/ area, ČLFA's /pro-cleny section, AKAT's Registrace/Přihlásit login and APEK's komunita.apek.cz, by asking each association's press office directly rather than probing. Then decide whether any warrants paid membership. For komunita.apek.cz specifically, first test Discourse's public .json endpoints — the empty body observed is an SPA artefact and is not by itself evidence of a gate.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical member rosters were not captured; only current-state snapshots were observed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull archived captures of the ČBA, ČLFA, AKAT and APEK member pages from the Wayback Machine to build a longitudinal entry/exit series, and in particular capture usfcr.cz before its rebrand to casfpz.cz and acss.cz before its move to stavebnisporitelny.cz. SBK's dated contributor-exclusion notes already provide a partial 2017-2024 exit log for the cards market and should be the template for what to reconstruct elsewhere.

coverage_gaps.description: Insurance and crypto-asset representation in the Czech financial-sector association map is unresolved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm ČAP (cap.cz) liveness with a browser-grade client and map its member registry and statistics, given bancassurance's weight in Czech bank fee income. Separately, establish whether a Czech crypto-asset service provider association exists under MiCA — if none does, record that absence explicitly so downstream cells do not keep searching for it.

coverage_gaps.description: Association working groups, committees and named officeholders were located but not harvested, leaving the people layer of the actor map empty.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest ČBA /o-nas/komise-pracovni-skupiny and /o-nas/organy, ČLFA /o-nas/organy-clfa and /o-nas/lide---vedeni-clfa, AKAT /Asociace-AKAT/Organy-asociace, AČSS 'Orgány AČSS' and the ČEFTAS board and FinTech Ambassador lists. Committee membership reveals which bank owns which regulatory or technical agenda, and officeholder names are the highest-yield search keys for finding executive statements that never appear in formal disclosures. Pair this with an annual sweep of the Card Forum / Card Session / Prague Payments Week / Acquiring Day speaker lists.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice has been confirmed reachable by an independent verification pass, and several were reached only via redirects or non-obvious entry points.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route every candidate URL through the deterministic liveness check, paying particular attention to: bankovnikarty.cz and cardmag.cz (root serves only a META-refresh shim — verify the /pages/... targets, not the root), acss.cz (redirects to stavebnisporitelny.cz), usfcr.cz (redirects to casfpz.cz), data.apek.cz (HTTP to HTTPS upgrade), and cap.cz (connection reset, expected to need a browser-grade client).

coverage_gaps.description: The mandatory Czech-language search sweep of the cell's seed queries was never executed because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted at the first call. Discovery ran entirely on direct fetch plus link-snowballing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search available, executing all six seed queries plus extensions in cs and en ('distribuce tiskových zpráv', 'rozeslání tiskové zprávy médiím', 'tiskové centrum banka', 'press release distribution Czech Republic financial'). Treat the current slice as a strong domain-led baseline to be widened, not as a completed pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Smaller and non-bank financial actors were not swept: credit unions (spořitelní a úvěrní družstva), small licensed payment institutions and e-money issuers, PSD2 third-party providers, and fintechs such as buy-now-pay-later and payment-gateway startups. Only Comgate was confirmed among pure-play PSPs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Take the ČNB list of licensed payment institutions and credit unions as the actor spine, then for each entity test (a) a newsroom path from its homepage and (b) a Protext keyword query. Entities with no newsroom become wire-only sources — the exact case this cell was created to catch.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language and international distribution of Czech financial announcements is unmapped. It is unknown whether Czech banks or PSPs use GlobeNewswire, Business Wire, PR Newswire or EQS for English releases, although Protext itself claims reach into media in nearly 180 countries and offers an English-language filter.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test the Protext search with jazyk=angličtina and původ=ČR to size the English-language Czech flow first, since that is free and confirmed. Then check whether PSE-listed financials route regulated announcements through a commercial international wire.

coverage_gaps.description: The downstream mirror graph is unmapped. Protext states distribution to 27 Czech news portals, and ceskenoviny.cz/pr/ was confirmed as one of them, but the other mirrors were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Obtain the portal list from the Protext client documentation, then verify each mirror. Mirrors matter for redundancy (if protext.cz blocks crawling) and for measuring pickup, and some mirrors retain items the origin later removes.

coverage_gaps.description: Four high-value targets are behind bot defences or transport failures and have no confirmed collection route: ČSOB (HTTP 500 on all paths), UniCredit Bank CZ (403), Banka CREDITAS (403), Mastercard CZ newsroom (403), plus Anopress and Monitora (TLS errors).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route all of these to a headless-browser collector with realistic headers and polite rate limits, and re-verify from a normal network before any is recorded as unreachable. For ČSOB in particular, stand up the Protext and KBC fallbacks now so the actor is not simply absent from the corpus.

coverage_gaps.description: Licensing terms for bulk collection are unresolved for every archive in this cell: ČTK/Protext content reuse, ČTK Infobanka, NEWTON Media archive (1989-present), Anopress and Monitora. Robots and terms-of-use were not inspected for protext.cz or ceskenoviny.cz.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before any production crawl, read robots.txt and terms for protext.cz and ceskenoviny.cz, and get written scope for what may be stored and redistributed. Default to storing metadata plus links and keeping full text internal-only until licensing is settled; for the commercial archives, buy access rather than scrape.

coverage_gaps.description: The PR-agency layer was identified (APRA member directory, Mediář agency index) but not harvested, so the mapping from agency to financial-sector client has not been built.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scrape the APRA member list and the Mediář agency index, then crawl each agency's references/case-study pages for Czech bank, insurer and payment-provider clients. This yields early warning of campaigns and a route to announcements that bypass corporate newsrooms.

coverage_gaps.description: Archive depth is confirmed only for a few sources (Protext finance category around 440 pages and roughly 50,525 total records; ČNB 1997-2026; MONETA back to about 2015; NEWTON archive advertised from 1989). Depth is unknown for KB, Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank, Air Bank, Fio and mBank CZ because their listings did not render.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: During the first headless crawl, record the oldest retrievable item per newsroom as a depth metric, and prioritise the ČTK wire for any period predating a given company's own archive.

coverage_gaps.description: No search-engine discovery was possible (WebSearch budget exhausted at 200/200 before this agent ran), so the six seed queries and their planned cs/en extensions were never executed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available, executing at minimum the six seed queries plus cs extensions on individual bank names in inflected form ('Komerční banka zisk', 'Česká spořitelna výsledky', 'ČSOB hospodářské výsledky', 'Moneta Money Bank čtvrtletí', 'Raiffeisenbank ČR zisk', 'Air Bank Partners banka', 'platební brána akvizice') and en extensions ('Czech bank profit Prague newspaper', 'Czech payments deal coverage English').

coverage_gaps.description: Two outlets explicitly named in the cell brief — iDNES Ekonomika and Lidovky — could not be reached at all because the fetch tool blocks the MAFRA hosts. Their RSS paths, section structure and paywall model are unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Verify both via the Chrome browser MCP or a plain HTTP client; specifically capture the ekonomika.idnes.cz RSS/servis feed path and the lidovky.cz ekonomika feed, and record the MAFRA Premium paywall boundary.

coverage_gaps.description: Broadcast and audio were only partially covered. ČT24's economy desk was verified, but Czech Radio's business output (Český rozhlas Plus / Radiožurnál business slots, ČRo's 'Zaostřeno'-style formats) and the fast-growing Czech business-podcast layer (HN podcasts, Seznam Zprávy podcasts, Info.cz's large podcast slate, CzechCrunch audio) were not mapped. Bank CEOs give figures and forward guidance in podcast interviews that appear nowhere in text.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map Český rozhlas business programming and the podcast feeds of HN, Seznam Zprávy, E15 (FLOW) and CzechCrunch; collect episode RSS with titles/descriptions and transcribe episodes featuring named bank or payment-firm executives.

coverage_gaps.description: Newsletter products were not mapped. Czech business newsrooms increasingly put their best analysis in paid newsletters (HN's business newsletters, Ekonom's Wednesday newsletter observed on-site, Deník N's 'Ranních 5 minut', E15 and CzechCrunch mailings) which are not on the public web and are not indexed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate and subscribe to the finance/business newsletters of the outlets in this slice; route them to a dedicated mailbox that the collector can parse.

coverage_gaps.description: No actor map of individual Czech banking/finance journalists was built (bylines, their outlet moves, and their personal X/LinkedIn/Bluesky accounts where scoops often break minutes before the article). MediaGuru was identified as the pointer that would support this but its /lide personnel feed was not mined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a named-journalist registry for the cell by harvesting bylines from the verified section listings over ~60 days, cross-checked against MediaGuru personnel news; then track their social accounts as an early-warning layer.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language CZ business coverage is thin in this slice: only Expats.cz was verified, Radio Prague International returned 403, and other English titles (Prague Morning, Brno Daily, the English output of Czech agencies) were not reachable without search.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: In a re-run, verify Prague Morning and Brno Daily, and check whether ČTK offers an English wire product; this matters for any downstream consumer who cannot read Czech.

coverage_gaps.description: Specialist finance/investment media that a naive scout would sweep up here — Patria.cz, Kurzy.cz, Investiční web, Roklen24, Měšec.cz, Peníze.cz, Bankovnípoplatky.com — were deliberately NOT claimed by this cell, which is scoped to general business/economic media. They were also not verified, so nothing should be assumed about them from this slice.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm that the specialist-finance-media cell in this run covers these domains; if no such cell exists, raise them for reassignment rather than leaving them uncovered.

coverage_gaps.description: The compliant full-text route for paywalled and print-only CZ coverage is unresolved. Newton Media was verified as offering a licensed CEE archive, but Monitora and Anopress could not be reached, and no pricing, API capability or redistribution terms were established for any of the three.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Request commercial terms from Newton Media (NewtonOne) and Monitora, and check whether Anopress is already available through a Czech university/National Library institutional subscription; compare against the cost of 3-4 direct publisher subscriptions (HN+/Ekonom bundle, E15 Premium, Deník N).

coverage_gaps.description: Virtually all Czech-segment data in this cell is locked inside PDFs (quarterly reports, presentation decks, URDs, country sheets). Only Erste (XLSX data sheets), KBC (results table / ESEF XBRL), RBI (XLSM) and SG (quarterly series) offer structured alternatives.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Prioritise the structured artefacts as the primary series feed and use PDFs only for narrative. Build a PDF table-extraction step specifically tuned to the KBC 'Czech Republic Business Unit' chapter and the Erste 'Czech Republic' segment tables, which are the two densest recurring sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage of this cell is structurally thin, as documented in the negative findings. cs-language terms were successfully used and did surface the relay layer and Czech-law prospectuses, but no parent publishes IR content in Czech.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Accept English as the primary language for this cell and use cs only for (a) subsidiary press-room relays, (b) prospectus/mandatory-disclosure trees on rb.cz, ppfbanka.cz, unicreditbank.cz, and (c) pse.cz / CNB issuer registers. Maintain a cs↔en glossary so the same event can be matched across both layers.

coverage_gaps.description: The CRD Article 89 country-by-country reporting annexes — which give Czech Republic turnover, profit before tax, tax paid and FTE headcount on a uniform basis across Erste, KBC, SG, UniCredit, RBI and BNP Paribas — were reasoned about and are known to sit in group annual reports/URDs, but the specific annex pages were not individually located and page-anchored in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each of the six groups, open the current annual report/URD and record the exact section title and page anchor for the country-by-country annex. This yields the single most directly comparable cross-parent Czech dataset in the whole cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth was only established for Erste (reports reportedly back to 1997) and Euronet (EDGAR filings back to at least 2004). Archive depth for KBC, SG, UniCredit, RBI, PPF and Worldline was not determined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a one-off backfill probe per parent against both the corporate IR archive and the relevant officially appointed mechanism (OeKB for AT, FSMA/STORI for BE, AMF/BDIF for FR, CONSOB eMarket for IT, AFM for NL) to establish the earliest retrievable year before committing to a time-series design.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the Austrian OAM (OeKB) was identified and verified. The equivalent statutory archives for the Belgian (KBC), French (SG, BNP Paribas, Worldline), Italian (UniCredit) and Dutch (PPF's former N.V. entities) parents were not located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify and add the Belgian FSMA, French AMF, Italian CONSOB/eMarket Storage and Dutch AFM regulated-information repositories as durable archive pointers, mirroring the role OeKB plays for Erste and RBI.

coverage_gaps.description: Two perimeter/identity changes in this cell threaten archive continuity: PPF Group N.V. became PPF GROUP a.s., and PPF Financial Holdings B.V. became PPF Financial Holdings a.s. Erste's acquisition of Santander Bank Polska (now Erste Bank Polska) also changes the segment mix against which the Czech segment is compared.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Record entity-identity mappings (old name, new name, jurisdiction, first/last reporting period) so time series are not silently broken, and flag Erste segment comparisons that straddle the Poland consolidation.

coverage_gaps.description: Two access frictions were observed or inferred: unicreditgroup.eu HTML pages appear WAF-protected (403), and the most analytically useful third-party layers (Patria research, Seeking Alpha, Quartr) are paywalled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision a browser-class fetcher with realistic headers for WAF-protected issuer sites, and treat paywalled research as out of scope for automated collection — rely on issuer-published webcast replays and free transcript feeds instead.

coverage_gaps.description: No keyword search of any kind was possible (WebSearch budget exhausted at the first call), so the six assigned seed queries were never run and no result-page snowballing occurred. Discovery relied entirely on URL hypothesis, first-principles category inference and on-page navigation snowballing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available and execute the six seed queries verbatim in Czech, plus extensions such as 'zmena sazebniku 2026 banka', 'rusi pobocky banka CR', 'sit bankomatu CR zmeny', 'srovnani poplatku bezny ucet', 'ceska banka rozhovor generalni reditel technologie'. Compare the resulting source set against this slice to measure the discovery bias introduced by the outage.

coverage_gaps.description: The English-language leg of the mandate is entirely unfulfilled. No en-language query was run, so English-language coverage of the Czech banking market - the trade press that writes about CEE banking in English, and English-language editions or summaries produced by Czech outlets - was not assessed at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run English queries on restoration: 'Czech Republic retail banking fees comparison portal', 'Czech banking trade magazine interview CEO digital', 'CEE banking trade press Czech banks fees ATM network', and check whether any of the confirmed Czech outlets (bankovnictvionline.cz, cc.cz) publish an English edition or English newsletter.

coverage_gaps.description: No Czech banking or personal-finance PODCAST, YouTube channel or newsletter-first publication was identified. Executive interviews about technology and payment strategy - exactly what the cell rationale calls out - increasingly appear in audio/video formats and in email-first products rather than on indexable article pages. Poradci-sobe.cz and profipf.cz were observed to carry podcast/video strands, and bankovnictvionline.cz has an app, but no standalone audio/video source was mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Czech podcast directories and YouTube for banking and fintech shows; check whether Bankovnictvi, CzechCrunch and Poradci-sobe podcast strands have their own feeds (RSS/Apple/Spotify) that can be transcribed and monitored independently of the article layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Branch-closure and ATM-network-change coverage is the weakest verified strand in this cell relative to how central the cell rationale makes it. bankovnipoplatky.cz's section listing mentions branch closures, and Mesec.cz's tables carry per-bank ATM withdrawal charges, but no source was found that systematically tracks Czech ATM COUNTS or branch counts over time. The Kurzy.cz /bankomaty/ vertical, which might do exactly this, did not render.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve the Kurzy.cz /bankomaty/ rendering question with a headless browser; separately look for a dedicated Czech ATM-locator or ATM-network dataset, and for coverage of the shared-ATM operators, which would be the actor to track for network consolidation.

coverage_gaps.description: The two highest-value institution-facing trade titles in this cell are subscription-gated: Bankovnictvi (bankovnictvionline.cz) shows preview excerpts with full text behind 'CELY CLANEK'/Predplatne, and PROFI Poradenstvi & Finance gates its magazine. FOND SHOP is likewise paywalled. The executive interviews that motivate this cell are therefore only partially readable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget for legitimate subscriptions to Bankovnictvi (offers a free sample issue to evaluate first) and to PROFI Poradenstvi & Finance. Do not attempt paywall circumvention. Meanwhile capture headline, dek, interviewee name, employer and role from the free index pages - that metadata alone supports an executive-and-topic tracking table.

coverage_gaps.description: RSS/feed availability was confirmed for exactly one source in this cell (Mesec.cz at https://www.mesec.cz/rss/clanky/, valid RSS 2.0, excerpt-only items). Every other candidate's feed status is unknown - most homepages advertise only email newsletters, and no /rss/ probing was done beyond Mesec.cz.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically probe /rss/, /rss/clanky/, /feed/ and /feed.xml on every confirmed domain in this slice, and parse each homepage's <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml> tags. Feed-based collection is far cheaper and far more robust than HTML scraping and would change the collection-method recommendation for most of these sources.

coverage_gaps.description: No Czech-language source dedicated to the MERCHANT/acquiring side of payments - payment terminals, card acceptance pricing, POS technology - was found as a specialist outlet. Podnikatel.cz is the closest proxy and covers it only incidentally; SystemOnLine covers bank-side IT rather than merchant acceptance. Given this run's payments scope, the acceptance layer is materially under-covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search for Czech retail/e-commerce trade media and acquiring-vendor publications ('platebni terminal', 'akceptace karet', 'akceptacni sit', 'QR platba', 'obchodnik prijem karet'), and check whether Czech e-commerce and retail trade titles carry a payments desk.

coverage_gaps.description: Publisher/operator identity is unresolved for two candidates that would otherwise rate higher: bankovnipoplatky.cz (no imprint surfaced on the pages fetched, despite it being the most on-topic fee watchdog in the cell) and fintechcowboys.cz (ownership not disclosed). Credibility scores for both are capped by this rather than by anything observed about their content.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the imprint/kontakt/o-nas pages and cross-check the operating entity in the Czech commercial register (justice.cz / ARES) before either source is weighted in analysis. Ownership matters especially for a fee watchdog, where a hidden commercial sponsor would invert the interpretation of its findings.

coverage_gaps.description: No search-engine-mediated discovery was possible in this run (WebSearch budget exhausted before the first call). Every source here was reached by guessing a domain or by snowballing from an already-known page, which structurally favours large incumbent outlets.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with WebSearch available, executing the six seed queries plus extensions, and specifically hunt the long tail: independent Czech fintech newsletters, Substack/LinkedIn-native commentators, and single-host podcasts. Treat the current slice as an incumbent-outlet baseline, not as complete coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: The 'fintech-focused podcasts' half of this cell is essentially unfilled. Only general-business and general-tech shows were confirmed (CzechCrunch Money Maker, Lupa.cz podcast, HN's MoneyPenny and Krypto Insider). No dedicated Czech fintech or payments podcast was verified, and the hypothesised association-linked 'FinTech Roadmap' show was not found on the association's site.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Czech podcast directories directly (Spotify, Apple Podcasts, mujRozhlas, Podbean) for 'fintech', 'platby', 'bankovnictví', 'finanční technologie'. Also check whether the Czech Fintech Association, ČSOB/Mastercard Fintech Challenge, or Fintech Week CEE run companion audio.

coverage_gaps.description: Six named targets could not be read: Forbes.cz (JS-rendered, empty bodies on three paths) plus five HTTP 403s (Peníze.cz, Investiční web, Živě.cz, Ecommerce Bridge CZ, Finmag.cz). Forbes CZ is named directly in the cell brief and Ecommerce Bridge is the only merchant-acceptance-side title identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a headless-browser fetch path to the collection stack and re-probe all six. For each, first check for sitemap.xml and RSS, which often bypass both JS rendering and bot walls. Do not mark any of them dead on the current evidence.

coverage_gaps.description: Four confirmed sources in this cell run subscription tiers whose gated content was never assessed: Hospodářské noviny+ (predplatne.hn.cz), e15 Premium (/e15-premium), Lupa+ (/podporte/), and the print/digital edition of Časopis Bankovnictví (/predplatne). The gated layer is likely where the substantive banking and vendor detail sits.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cost out subscriptions for HN+ and Časopis Bankovnictví as the two highest-value paid tiers for Czech banking and payments, and confirm each publisher's terms on machine collection of subscribed content before ingesting. Never circumvent a paywall.

coverage_gaps.description: Every confirmed outlet is Prague-centred national media. No regional Czech startup or tech media were identified — Brno (a substantial tech hub, and the venue for the CryptoNight event the association listed), Ostrava and Plzeň all have startup ecosystems whose local coverage was not probed at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe regional titles and hub publications (e.g. JIC Brno, TechTower Ostrava, regional Deník business sections) for payments/fintech content once search is restored. Regional coverage is where a young company appears before national media notices it — precisely this cell's stated weak-signal rationale.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Czech payments rests on two pan-regional outlets (Tech.eu, The Recursive) whose Czech output is intermittent and skewed toward VC deal news. No Czech-domiciled English-language business publication was identified, and CzechCrunch showed no English edition in the structure retrieved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe for English editions or English tags on Czech outlets, and check whether Czech banks, payment institutions and the Czech Fintech Association publish English press rooms directly — for A1 disclosure topics, an English IR/press page on the actor's own site would be a direct source and outrank both aggregators.

coverage_gaps.description: No Czech VC-published or data-provider-published funding report was located. The depo.ventures hypothesis failed at DNS, and no equivalent Czech startup funding report publisher was confirmed. CzechStartups.gov.cz has a /startup-data/ path that was seen referenced but not itself retrieved and parsed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch and parse https://czechstartups.gov.cz/startup-data/ directly, and identify Czech VC funds that publish periodic ecosystem reports (via the /startup-ekosystem/investori/ directory, which lists 44 investors). A quantified Czech fintech funding series would anchor the qualitative media signal from this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: The Czech terminology used was derived from site navigation rather than tested for precision and recall. High-precision regulatory and acceptance-side terms — 'platební instituce', 'poskytovatel platebních služeb', 'licence ČNB', 'akvirer', 'POS terminál', 'okamžité platby', 'otevřené bankovnictví', 'PSD2' — were never run against any index, while the high-recall term 'platby' demonstrably returns noise.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and empirically test a two-tier Czech glossary (high-precision regulatory/technical terms vs high-recall broad terms) against Lupa's /n/ archives and CzechCrunch on-site search, recording hit counts and false-positive rates per term before wiring any keyword filter into production collection.

coverage_gaps.description: No search-engine querying occurred in this slice (WebSearch budget exhausted before the first call), so the cell was covered by seed-actor fetching and snowballing only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell (#23) with a fresh WebSearch budget and execute the six seed queries plus cs-language extensions such as 'analytik banka cílová cena zvýšil', 'ratingová agentura potvrdila rating české banky', 'konsensus analytiků výsledky KB', 'investiční doporučení bankovní sektor ČR'.

coverage_gaps.description: Moody's, S&P and Fitch are all blocked to unauthenticated automated fetch, leaving the rating-action layer of this cell undelivered despite being its highest-credibility component.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up authenticated headless-browser sessions with free registrations for each agency, and in parallel resolve ESMA's European Rating Platform as a licence-clean alternative. Route all three through access review before automated collection, since agency ToS generally forbid redistribution of press-release text.

coverage_gaps.description: ESMA's European Rating Platform and CEREP could not be located; three hostname/path guesses failed and the confirmed ESMA CRA hub does not link them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search ESMA's 'Databases and Registers' section directly, or query the ESMA site search for 'European Rating Platform'. Confirm whether the ERP offers bulk download or an API covering Czech bank issuers, then promote it as a direct candidate.

coverage_gaps.description: Only three Czech-market listed banks (Komerční banka, Moneta Money Bank, Erste/Česká spořitelna) have identifiable analyst-coverage pages. Large unlisted Czech banks — ČSOB (KBC), Raiffeisenbank CZ, UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, Air Bank/Home Credit, Fio banka, Trinity Bank — have no equity analyst layer and are visible to this cell only through rating actions and press mirrors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For unlisted Czech banks, pivot the collection design from equity research to (a) rating-agency issuer pages and (b) parent-group analyst coverage (KBC, Raiffeisen Bank International, UniCredit). Add parent-group research desks to the actor map for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: No Czech-language rating-agency commentary or local rating agency was identified. Historic Czech agencies (e.g. CRA Rating Agency, later absorbed into Moody's) and any smaller ESMA-registered agencies rating Czech institutions were not investigated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the ESMA registered-CRA list and its annual market-share document, then check each smaller registered agency (e.g. Scope Ratings, Creditreform, EuroRating) for Czech bank coverage — these are frequently free-to-read and unblocked, unlike the big three.

coverage_gaps.description: The run scope is sector=both, but every candidate found is banking-equity or bank-rating oriented. No sell-side or rating coverage of Czech payments actors (card schemes, PSPs, acquirers such as ČSOB/Global Payments JV, Comgate, GoPay) was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend cs queries toward payments-specific analyst language ('platební instituce', 'akvirer', 'zpracovatel plateb', 'fintech analýza ČR') and check whether payments firms appear in broker notes only via parent-bank coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Legal status is 'unclear' or 'restricted' for nearly every candidate. Patria, Kurzy.cz and Akcie.cz terms of service were not read, and rating-agency press releases carry explicit redistribution restrictions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch and record robots.txt and ToS for patria.cz, kurzy.cz and akcie.cz before any scheduled crawl, and set a default retention policy of metadata-plus-link for all third-party research text until licensing is cleared.

coverage_gaps.description: Zero Czech-language discovery was performed for this cell because the session-wide web-search budget was exhausted before the agent's first query. The cell's own Czech seed query was never run, and no Czech glossary/actor-map terms were exercised against a search engine.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available, executing the Czech seed query and Czech-language probes for foreign coverage of Czech banks (e.g. terms around foreign media, acquisition and results announcements in Czech). At minimum, run a Czech-language sweep for pointer pages that list which international outlets cover Czech finance.

coverage_gaps.description: Six candidates (Reuters, Bloomberg, The Banker, Radio Prague International, CEE Legal Matters, FinTech Futures, plus MarketScreener and the intellinews Czech country page) could not be inspected due to 403s or tool-level domain blocks. Their section URLs, feed availability and paywall mechanics are unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Have the deterministic verification pass retry these hosts with browser-like headers and, where still blocked, record them as access-restricted-but-live. Do not mark any of them dead on the single failed fetch recorded here.

coverage_gaps.description: Paid English deal-intelligence and filings-aggregation services that would systematically capture Czech banking M&A and licence events - Mergermarket/ION Analytics, LSEG/Refinitiv Deals, S&P Capital IQ, Dealogic, PitchBook - were not assessed at all this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass on commercial deal databases, assessing licence cost, Czech financial-sector coverage depth and whether an existing organisational subscription already provides access.

coverage_gaps.description: No per-issuer mapping was built. Which specific Czech banking and payments entities each international outlet actually names - and therefore which entities are reliably visible in English at all - remains unknown, since entity-level searching was impossible.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Once search is available, run entity-name probes for the major Czech banking groups and payment institutions against each confirmed outlet's on-site search (Emerging Europe and PYMNTS both expose working ?s= endpoints) and record hit counts per outlet as a coverage matrix.

coverage_gaps.description: Feed availability is confirmed for only one outlet in this cell, and no robots.txt or rate-limit posture was checked for any domain.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: During verification, probe standard feed paths (/feed/, /rss, /rss.xml, category+/feed/) for the WordPress-style sites and fetch robots.txt for every candidate domain before any scheduled polling is configured.

coverage_gaps.description: The statutory basis for the cell ended on 30.6.2025 and the successor (EBA Pillar 3 Data Hub) covers a different, CRR-scoped population — 'large and other institutions' — which will not include every small Czech bank, building society or credit union currently in the cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mirror the complete historical archive from every institution now, before pages are retired; then split the collector into two tracks — (a) national voluntary disclosures with per-entity continuity monitoring, (b) EBA P3DH for the in-scope institutions — and reconcile the two populations against the ČNB bank and credit-union indexes each quarter.

coverage_gaps.description: Five institution pages (ČSOB, ČSOB Hypoteční banka, UniCredit, Banka CREDITAS, ČSOB Stavební spořitelna) refused automated fetches with 403/500, and two more (Česká spořitelna, Air Bank) require JavaScript rendering. That is seven of the largest names in the sector, including two of the four systemically important banks.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a headless-browser collection tier with realistic headers and per-domain throttling before attempting production collection for this cell; verify each blocked URL in a real browser first and record the working deep link.

coverage_gaps.description: Three ČNB link-indexes (investment companies, pension companies, and 25 of the 35 securities dealers) and the EBA P3DH public portal remain unenumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Expand the securities-dealer index in full and tag the payments/FX-relevant firms; enumerate the P3DH country filter for CZ and test whether a bulk export or API exists.

coverage_gaps.description: The building-society tier (stavební spořitelny) was covered opportunistically via the ČNB index rather than through its own local-language search sweep, and two of its five members (ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida) could not be reached at all. Group consolidation is actively moving these entities onto parent-bank domains (Buřinka→burinka.csas.cz, Modrá pyramida→KB infrastructure, ČMSS→csobstavebni.cz), so their disclosure locations are unusually volatile.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated local-language pass on 'stavební spořitelna povinně uveřejňované informace / informace dle vyhlášky ČNB / čtvrtletní údaje', confirm the current deep link for all five societies in a real browser, and set a shorter re-resolution interval for this tier than for banks.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell is overwhelmingly Czech-only by legal design — the decree required publication in Czech — and no English mirror of the quarterly template was found at any Czech-owned institution. The only English-language disclosures observed were at the third-country branches (Bank of Communications Prague, in English and Chinese) and in some parallel annual reports (Trinity Bank, RSTS).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do not budget for English versions of the quarterly set; plan for Czech-language column-header normalisation in the parser, with a fixed CZ→EN field mapping derived from Annex 10, and use the third-country branches' English files as a Rosetta stone for that mapping.

coverage_gaps.description: No web-archive fallback was identified for this cell. Given that entities are demonstrably disappearing (Max banka, and disclosure pages being folded into parent-bank domains), and that the legal duty to keep publishing has lapsed, historical quarters are at real risk of vanishing without a snapshot.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a Wayback Machine / Common Crawl lookup step for every institution URL in the cell, and proactively submit each current disclosure page for archiving as part of the first collection run.

coverage_gaps.description: The comparability claim underpinning the cell — that the template is machine-comparable across all institutions — has not been tested against actual files, across issuers or across the 2014/2017/2021 amendments.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download one XLSX per institution class and per decree vintage, diff the sheet and column structure, and document which annexes carry ownership, organisational chart, branch counts and headcount before committing to a parser design.

coverage_gaps.description: The Burzovní věstník (ftp.pse.cz/Vestnik.doc) and the issuer master-data branch (ftp.pse.cz/Issuers.dta) are 401-gated, removing the exchange's authoritative gazette from automated reach.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retry both over https and with a standard browser user-agent to test whether the 401 is a WAF artefact; if it persists, contact BCPP (info@pse.cz, +420 221 832 820) to ask whether the Věstník and issuer master data are available publicly elsewhere or under a data agreement. Test whether individual files under those branches are reachable even when the listing is not.

coverage_gaps.description: The JSON/XHR endpoint that backs the BCPP news search and the Event Calendar was not identified, so the two most time-sensitive surfaces in this cell currently have no cheap collection route.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Open /novinky and /en/event-calendar in a real browser with the network panel recording, capture the underlying request URLs and parameters (including the PSE/ČTK source flag and the date range), and document them for the collector. Also test whether the calendar's Google/Outlook export produces a fetchable ICS URL.

coverage_gaps.description: Several ftp.pse.cz branches with recent modification dates were not opened in this run: Cdcp.dta, IssuersCDCP.dta, Member.dta, Results.act, Results.ak, Results.old, Service.dta, Tom.dta, Info.bas/CEEplus (mtime Aug 2026), Info.bas/Indexy (Jul 2026), Info.bas/RTS_27, Info.bas/XETRA_T7, Info.bas/Eng, Info.bas/Statistiky, and Info.bas/News subfolders including a 2025-09-01 directory.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do a single polite recursive enumeration of the whole ftp.pse.cz tree to produce a file manifest with sizes and mtimes, then classify which branches carry issuer-level content (as opposed to trading/technical data) and which are actually maintained. RTS_27 in particular should be checked as a MiFID II execution-quality source.

coverage_gaps.description: Files in Annual.rep and Semiannual.rep are named by abbreviated BCPP issuer codes (ICBA, RZBCL, CSPOL, TRIREL, CEZ, KOFOL, TELECL, …) rather than ISINs, and no public code→issuer→ISIN mapping table was located. Without it, the two largest filing archives cannot be reliably filtered to financial-sector issuers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the mapping by joining the archive file names against the Official Price List, the four market-data segment lists and the debt-securities lists across several historical dates; where a code cannot be resolved (typically delisted issuers), fall back to opening the PDF's cover page. Confirm whether Issuers.dta, once accessible, supplies this mapping directly.

coverage_gaps.description: The ČNB OAM/CÚRI repository was identified and its legal basis and content categories confirmed, but its search form, per-issuer result URL structure, pagination, and any bulk/export capability were not exercised in this run — only the entry-point URLs were captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one hands-on session against https://oam.cnb.cz/sipresextdad/SIPRESWEB.WEB21.START_INPUT_OAM?p_lang=cz for a known filer (Komerční banka or Moneta) to document the form fields, session behaviour, result URL shape and whether an English interface (p_lang=en) exists; check the legacy p_hist=A system for pre-August-2009 coverage of Czech bank filings.

coverage_gaps.description: START-market disclosure material is predominantly Czech-only: the Start Day presentations, the PX Veřejná nabídka user guide and description (both May 2025) and the sponsored analytical reports have no confirmed English counterparts, while only the older START public-offering rules (v2.0, Nov 2020) exist in English. Coverage of the SME/fintech tripwire therefore depends entirely on Czech-language collection.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Set Czech as the mandatory collection language for the START branch and budget for machine translation of presentation PDFs; do not rely on /en/ mirrors, which lag or omit START content.

coverage_gaps.description: The debt-securities segment lists name the bank issuers (Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit Bank, J&T Banka, J&T Finance Group) but were not traced through to each issuer's prospectus, base prospectus, or issuer-level disclosure pages. These are exactly the banks that carry disclosure duty without listed equity, so the linkage is the highest-value unfinished work in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each bond ISIN on the financial-sector and other-bonds lists, pull /detail/{ISIN} for the issuer identity, then locate the prospectus via the ČNB prospectus register and the issuer's own IR site, and register each bank as a monitored entity independent of its equity-listing status.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's core premise — that the exchange timestamp is worth having because IR pages get edited or withdrawn — has no baseline: no snapshot of BCPP announcement text versus issuer IR text has been taken, so divergence cannot yet be detected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For the three Prime-listed banks, snapshot the BCPP announcement, the ČNB OAM filing and the issuer's own IR item for the same event over one reporting cycle, and measure timing and wording divergence. That baseline determines how much collection weight each of the three channels deserves.

coverage_gaps.description: The ČNB Central Storage (OAM) offers no documented API, RSS feed or bulk export; it is a form-driven Oracle web application. Every regulated filing must be reached through session-bound queries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a resilient session-aware crawler with issuer-dropdown enumeration and date-window paging, plus checkpointing. In parallel, ask ČNB directly (the site publishes a §106 information-request channel) whether a machine-readable export or feed of OAM content exists, and set a watch on ESAP onboarding as the eventual replacement.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell established WHERE the CZ payment institution / EMI / small-scale PSP registers live (JERRS, PSRI list, EBA PSD2 register) but did not extract the actual entity roster or counts, and did not confirm which JERRS role codes correspond to each of the four Czech payments licence categories.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated extraction pass that enumerates JERRS role categories, records the exact Czech role labels and their identifiers, and produces a reconciled CZ payments entity list joined against the ČNB PSRI list and the EBA register.

coverage_gaps.description: JERRS presents current status (valid / suspended / revoked) and offers aggregate counts and creation/termination time series, but it is unclear whether per-entity historical states (previous names, past authorisation scopes, withdrawal dates) are retrievable retrospectively.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Start snapshotting the open-data CSVs and JERRS category listings weekly from day one to build an internal point-in-time history, rather than assuming ČNB can reconstruct it later. Test whether WS JERRS returns authorisation date ranges and prior states.

coverage_gaps.description: English interfaces exist for OAM (/cnb/oam_en), JERRS (/cnb/jerrs_en) and the ČNB lists hub, but whether the English content and lists are updated in step with the Czech originals was not tested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Collect the Czech versions as the authoritative record and use the English versions only for label mapping; run a one-off content-parity check on a sample of entities and filings before relying on any EN page as a data source.

coverage_gaps.description: Branches of foreign banks and passported EEA payment institutions operating in CZ typically disclose in their home member state's OAM rather than in the ČNB storage, and this cell did not map which CZ-active entities fall into that category or where their filings actually land.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use the ČNB 'banky a pobočky zahraničních bank' open dataset and the EBA registers to segment CZ-active entities into domestic filers versus home-state filers, then record the corresponding foreign OAMs as separate sources in a later pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Registers of pověření zástupci (payment service agents), vázaní zástupci and samostatní zprostředkovatelé — fed through REGIS and surfaced in JERRS and the open data — were identified but not enumerated. These reveal distribution networks and white-label payment arrangements that are otherwise invisible.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated extraction of the agent/representative lists (including the WS JERRS representatives operation and the EBA agent data) as a follow-on task; they are high-volume and need their own change-detection cadence.

coverage_gaps.description: The date coverage of the ČNB prospectus register and of the final-terms register was not established — in particular whether records predating Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 (i.e. pre-July 2019 approvals under the old prospectus directive regime) remain searchable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe both registers with wide historical date ranges and a known older Czech bank bond programme to establish the earliest retrievable record, and document the cut-off in the source register.

coverage_gaps.description: Ultimate beneficial ownership for Czech payment institutions, processors and vendors is no longer obtainable from a free public source after the 17 December 2025 closure of the ESM public part and its open data.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide an access route and get it approved: (a) test whether the organisation qualifies as an AML-obliged entity for the announced automated remote-access form, (b) price a commercial provider (Dun & Bradstreet CZ, CRIF/CRIBIS) that retains ownership trees and pre-2025 snapshots, and (c) meanwhile fall back on úplný výpis shareholder history plus 'zpráva o vztazích' related-party reports in the deeds collection.

coverage_gaps.description: There is no machine-readable index or bulk feed of the Sbírka listin documents, and the only official web path is rate-limited (3000 requests/day, max 50/minute) with random CAPTCHA challenges, per the ministry's published operating conditions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Design the collector around a persistent IČO->subjektId->spis map plus an annual/quarterly delta sweep within those limits; in parallel write to the Ministry of Justice (odbor informatiky) asking about higher-volume access under the 'written guarantees' clause in the operating conditions, and evaluate a licensed mirror as fallback.

coverage_gaps.description: The ISVR bulk open data carries a stated non-commercial usage condition and contains personal data making the recipient a GDPR controller, which is unresolved for a commercial market-intelligence use case.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Obtain legal sign-off on the ISVR open-data terms before bulk ingestion; if commercial use is not covered, restrict the pipeline to per-entity public register lookups and the ARES REST API (whose published conditions set only volume limits) and document that decision in the source registry.

coverage_gaps.description: Deeds filings are PDFs, frequently scanned images, and are legally required to be in Czech; there is no structured XBRL-style financial feed for unlisted Czech entities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget an OCR + Czech-language table-extraction stage (rozvaha / výkaz zisku a ztráty / příloha v účetní závěrce) with a validated mapping to a common financial schema, and consider buying pre-parsed financials (Merk, CRIBIS, D&B) for breadth while parsing only strategically important filings in-house.

coverage_gaps.description: Small and micro entities file abbreviated statements (zkrácený rozsah) that may omit the profit-and-loss detail, and many small vendors omit or delay filing entirely despite the sanction regime; foreign banks and EU-passporting payment providers operating in CZ through a branch (odštěpný závod) or on a freedom-of-services basis may file little or nothing in the Czech deeds collection.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Flag every actor with an expected-but-missing or abbreviated filing, enrich size from the statistical register (RES employee bands) and VAT status, and for passporting/branch players route to the home-country register via BRIS and to the ČNB notification lists instead of expecting a Czech filing.

coverage_gaps.description: Documents in the collection of deeds must be drawn up and lodged in Czech, so essentially the entire disclosure corpus for this cell is Czech-only; the English-language layer is limited to guides and to a few large banks' voluntary English annual reports.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Czech as the working language of this cell: maintain the Czech filing-label glossary (účetní závěrka, výroční zpráva, zpráva auditora, zpráva o vztazích, rozvaha, výkaz zisku a ztráty, příloha) as the parser's key vocabulary, and machine-translate only for downstream reporting, never for matching.

coverage_gaps.description: Filing timing creates a structural lag: statements are approved within 6 months and filed within 12 months of period end, and late filing is common, so the deeds collection is a 6-18 month-old view and cannot support earnings-cycle or quarterly monitoring.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Schedule the collector for a main annual sweep (mid-year through year-end for the prior financial year) plus monthly catch-up passes for late filers, and pair this cell with faster channels (regulator statistics, press releases, listed-bank IR) for anything time-sensitive.

coverage_gaps.description: The actor universe for this cell has not yet been enumerated: the NACE-code and regulator-list sweeps that would turn the register into a concrete list of CZ banking/payments companies and their suppliers were designed but not executed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run two sweeps and store the resulting IČO list: (1) ČNB JERRS export of banks, payment institutions, small-scale providers, e-money institutions and agents; (2) ARES POST /vyhledat filtered on CZ-NACE 6419, 6499, 6612, 6619, 6209, 6311 and on Czech name tokens ('platební', 'platebn', 'karty', 'terminál', 'bankomat', 'processing'). Then resolve each to subjektId and pull the deeds list.

coverage_gaps.description: Most Czech bank EUR covered bonds and MREL paper carry XS identifiers, and Česká spořitelna's inaugural covered bond is listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange regulated market (with at least one AT-prefixed ČS instrument observed, AT0000A2STV4). The disclosure pages of the foreign listing venues — Wiener Börse, and the Luxembourg / Euronext Dublin venues typically used for XS paper — were not enumerated in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over Wiener Börse, Luxembourg Stock Exchange and Euronext Dublin issuer/security pages for the six licensed Czech covered-block issuers plus MONETA and Raiffeisenbank, keyed on the ISINs already extracted from the ČNB register; these venues host prospectus repositories and ongoing-disclosure notices that mirror or supplement issuer sites.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the six ČNB-licensed covered-block issuers plus Banka CREDITAS were mapped. Other Czech deposit-takers with MREL obligations and likely bond issuance — Air Bank / PPF banka, J&T Banka, Fio banka, Trinity Bank, Max banka — and the building societies (Českomoravská stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna) were not systematically searched. PPF banka already surfaced as a prospectus host in one result set.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query each institution in Czech with the pattern '<banka> povinně uveřejňované informace dluhopisy emise prospekt' and '<banka> MREL dluhopisy emise', and independently sweep the ČNB final-terms register filtered to credit-institution issuers to catch any bank missed by name-based searching.

coverage_gaps.description: No aggregate time series of Czech covered-bond / HZL outstanding volumes was located. ČNB ARAD is the obvious candidate database but was not reached before the search budget ran out; the CDCP Fact Book and the ECBC Fact Book Czech chapter are partial substitutes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search ČNB ARAD in Czech for 'hypoteční zástavní listy' and 'kryté dluhopisy' series, and check the ČNB financial-market statistics section, so issuer-level cover-pool data can be normalised against a market total.

coverage_gaps.description: Both ČNB registers that matter most here — the prospectus register and the final-terms register — are served by a legacy Oracle PL/SQL web application (oam.cnb.cz/sipresextdad/SIPRESWEB...) with form-driven input and no observed API, JSON endpoint, RSS or bulk export. The covered-block issuer list is a hand-maintained PDF.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a resilient scraper with a headless-browser fallback and a stable ISIN/LEI/IČO join key; hash the covered-block PDF for change detection. Also test whether ESMA's EU-level prospectus register mirrors ČNB approvals, which would give a cleaner feed for the same content.

coverage_gaps.description: Moody's and S&P covered-bond analytics for Czech programmes (ČS's inaugural bond is Moody's Aaa; KB is Fitch AAA) sit largely behind registration or subscription. Only the Fitch rating-action headline linked from KB's own investor page was reachable in this run.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Register for free agency accounts to obtain rating-action press releases and performance-overview summaries, and treat issuer-page rating links (as on KB's covered bond page) as the reliable free entry point. Do not plan on systematic extraction of full agency reports.

coverage_gaps.description: Transaction announcements from deal counsel and arrangers (A&O Shearman on both the ČS EUR 500m inaugural covered bond and a UniCredit CZ&SK EUR 500m mortgage covered bond issuance; bookrunner line-ups disclosed via broker notes) proved to be a fast, well-dated channel that often describes programme structure before the issuer publishes anything. Only incidental examples were captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a standing sweep of the Czech capital-markets practice news feeds (A&O Shearman, Clifford Chance, White & Case, Kinstellar, PRK Partners, Allen Overy CZ) and of the British Chamber of Commerce CZ and Czech Banking Association news pages, filtered on 'covered bond', 'krytý dluhopis', 'MREL', to catch deal announcements at T+0.

coverage_gaps.description: Four of the nine ČNB-listed pension companies — Allianz, UNIQA, Conseq and Rentea penzijní společnost — were captured only via the ČNB index entry and were not individually profiled or fetched in this pass. Rentea in particular is a newer entrant whose distribution model has not been characterised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch each of the four disclosure URLs from the ČNB pension index, confirm the annual-report location and format, and add them as candidates so the third-pillar entity set is complete before any market-share reasoning is attempted.

coverage_gaps.description: The ČNB investiční společnosti index as fetched returned only eight entities and included 'AXA investiční společnost a.s.', a name superseded by the UNIQA rebrand, while omitting REICO investiční společnost České spořitelny, which other sources show still exists. The list is therefore either partially stale or truncated in retrieval, so the bank-group investment-company population cannot be treated as settled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Rebuild the investment-company and investment-firm population from JERRS / WS JERRS rather than from the HTML disclosure indexes, and reconcile the two lists; add REICO and any other ČS/KB/UniCredit/Raiffeisen-group managers found.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell definition frames credit unions as sitting 'inside the same banking groups' as the other entity types. Nothing found supports this for CZ: all six ČNB-indexed spořitelní družstva (Artesa, Citfin, České spořitelní družstvo, NEY, Peněžní dům, Podnikatelská družstevní záložna) appear to be standalone cooperatives, not bank-group subsidiaries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat CZ credit unions as an independent comparator segment rather than a window into banking-group strategy, and reallocate expected analytical weight toward building societies, pension companies and in-group investment firms, which genuinely are group subsidiaries.

coverage_gaps.description: No check was made of whether historical annual-report PDFs remain retrievable after site migrations. Two migrations are already visible in this cell (ČMSS to csobstavebni.cz, burinka.cz to burinka.csas.cz) and a third is in progress (modrapyramida.cz to KB infrastructure), each of which typically prunes older documents.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Back-fill and mirror the full available archives now — Buřinka's 2000–2025 series and Raiffeisen's 2020–2025 bilingual set are the priorities — and record Wayback Machine snapshots for the migrating domains before older files disappear.

coverage_gaps.description: Parent-group reporting that describes these CZ subsidiaries — KBC/ČSOB, Erste Group/Česká spořitelna, Société Générale-lineage KB, Raiffeisen Bank International, Generali CEE — was touched only incidentally through KBC group annual reports surfaced in English search, and not systematically mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm with the run coordinator whether parent-group IR belongs to another coverage cell; if not, add the five group IR sites as indirect sources, since group reports date CZ subsidiary restructurings and IT programmes that the local entity report describes only after the fact.

coverage_gaps.description: Several candidate URLs were carried forward from the ČNB indexes without an independent fetch — notably ČSOB Asset Management, Generali Investments CEE, Amundi CZ, NEY, Peněžní dům, Podnikatelská družstevní záložna and České spořitelní družstvo. Their document depth, formats and update cadence are therefore unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over every candidate URL and example URL in this slice, and treat any 403 or timeout as bot defence to be retried with a browser-grade client rather than as evidence the source is dead.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's entities have changed names and legal perimeters: Českomoravská záruční a rozvojová banka (ČMZRB) -> Národní rozvojová banka (NRB); Fond pojištění vkladů -> Garanční systém finančního trhu (GSFT, from 1.1.2016 under Act 374/2015 Sb., now holding both FPV and FŘK); and ČEB is being absorbed as an NRB subsidiary. Procurement platforms still file NRB under the legacy 'CMZRB' authority code.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and store an explicit alias/lineage table keyed by IČO (NRB 44848943, ČNB 48136450, ČEB 63078333, SFPI 70856788, plus EGAP and GSFT identifiers to be captured) covering former names, acronyms, English-in-Czech forms and legacy platform codes, and apply it to every query and dedupe step.

coverage_gaps.description: Contracting-authority profiles were positively located for NRB (TenderArena + NEN + own page) and ČNB (E-ZAK + vhodne-uverejneni.cz), and a procurement page was located for ČEB. No procurement profile was located for EGAP, GSFT, PGRLF or the Kancelář finančního arbitra in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run an IČO-keyed sweep across Věstník veřejných zakázek, NEN, TenderArena, E-ZAK instances, gemin.cz and vhodne-uverejneni.cz for every remaining in-cell entity, and record which platform each authority actually uses. Treat Registr smluv as the backstop, since contract publication is mandatory even where a tender profile is hard to find.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell is dominated by annual publications. Apart from MF's monthly ownership snapshots, NRB's Pillar 3 disclosures, GSFT prospectus supplements and the press feeds, there is little sub-annual quantitative disclosure — and no first-party API from any core entity.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Anchor sub-annual monitoring on four cross-cutting routes instead: (1) psp.cz full-text for EGAP/ČEB/ČNB parliamentary submissions, (2) Registr smluv new-contract feeds by IČO, (3) NRB CRR 575/2013 quarterly/semi-annual disclosures, (4) GSFT bond-programme prospectuses and supplements, which restate fund balances for investors between annual reports.

coverage_gaps.description: GSFT annual reports and budgets give fund positions in PDF form, but no structured time series of Fond pojištění vkladů / Fond pro řešení krize balances, contribution rates or covered-deposit base was identified — for example in the CNB ARAD statistical database or an EU-level dataset (EBA deposit-guarantee data, EFDI).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe CNB ARAD for a deposit-insurance or covered-deposits series, and check EBA's published DGS funds-available data and EFDI membership pages for a machine-readable Czech series that can be joined to the GSFT PDFs.

coverage_gaps.description: NRB operates as a national promotional bank alongside EIF/EIB, InvestEU and Modernisation Fund instruments, and appears in at least one European Commission transport-facility programme fiche; EGAP operates within the OECD Arrangement on Officially Supported Export Credits and Berne Union reporting. None of these supranational counterpart sources were worked in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up sweep of EIF/EIB counterpart announcements and InvestEU implementing-partner disclosures naming NRB, plus OECD export-credit and Berne Union statistics naming Czechia, as an indirect route that quantifies programme volumes independently of the Czech institutions' own reporting.

coverage_gaps.description: Czech terminology was established for annual reporting, disclosure, procurement, guarantees and deposit insurance. It was NOT established for the internal operating/vendor vocabulary these institutions use in tenders — e.g. core banking, card issuing/acquiring, ATM and self-service estate, payment terminal servicing, document management — which is the vocabulary a procurement-focused sweep actually needs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before the collection run, mine 20-30 actual tender titles from the NRB TenderArena/NEN profiles and ČNB E-ZAK to extract real Czech procurement phrasing and CPV codes, then feed those verbatim terms back into search rather than translating English vendor terminology into Czech.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage focused on national-level institutions. Regional development funds, the Czech-Moravian Guarantee scheme's regional arms, Národní rozvojový fond, and municipal/regional co-financing vehicles that partner with commercial banks were not surveyed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from the NRB 'Naši partneři / přehled institucí' page and from the MF and MPO ownership registers to enumerate second-tier public financial vehicles, then triage them by whether they publish an annual report and whether they name partner banks.

briefs: The four systemic Czech banks do not form the symmetric IR estate the cell brief assumed. Komerční banka is the only one with locally listed equity and it behaves accordingly: a complete IR hub with a results archive back to 2000 carrying presentations, IFRS statements and machine-readable facts-and-figures spreadsheets, ESEF/XBRL annual reports back to 2020, a financial calendar, a ratings page and a full general-meeting record — comfortably the richest single node in the cell. The other three publish locally only what statute requires: Česká spořitelna routes everything through a JavaScript document repository with stable numeric category IDs, ČSOB publishes results as dated tzYYMMDD.pdf press releases plus a late-April annual report, and UniCredit Bank CZ&SK offers annual and half-year PDFs on a fully templatable CDN path with no Czech-language IR page at all. Their analytical layer lives at the parents, so Erste Group and KBC Group are not optional extras but load-bearing sources for ČS and ČSOB respectively, each publishing a quarterly Czech Republic segment. Two collection caveats dominate: csob.cz returned HTTP 500 and unicreditbank.cz HTTP 403 on every HTML fetch this session while their PDFs remain search-indexed, so both are bot-defended-but-live hypotheses for the verification pass rather than dead sources; and UniCredit Bank CZ&SK's figures are a merged Czech-Slovak entity that must be segmented before any CZ market sizing.

The Czech second tier splits sharply into one issuer-grade disclosure machine and a long tail of statutory-minimum filers: MONETA Money Bank runs a full bilingual IR operation (quarterly presentations, transcripts, webcasts, XLSX data packs, IR calendar, sell-side previews from Fio's desk and a Prague Stock Exchange record), while Raiffeisenbank CZ sits in between with half-year reports, a country-level investor presentation and RBI group segment reporting behind it. Everyone else — Air Bank, Fio banka, Banka CREDITAS, Trinity Bank, Partners Banka — publishes annual reports plus ČNB/ČBA-format quarterly annexes and a press room, with Fio's and Trinity's .xlsx annexes and Partners Banka's superseded-document archive the most machine-friendly material in the cell; parent groups (PPF for Air Bank, mBank S.A. for the Czech branch, Partners Financial Services with its growth prospectus) carry the narrative the local entities omit. The regulator is the key that unlocks all of it: the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure URLs resolves eight of the ten named actors in a single fetch, with JERRS, the Central Repository of Regulated Information and or.justice.cz Sbírka listin as the authoritative backstops. Two caveats dominate the cell — the roster is stale, since Max banka has merged into Banka CREDITAS (maxbanka.eu now a closing historical archive) and Hello bank has exited the Czech market entirely, while mBank as an EU single-licence branch files no Czech statutory report at all — and collection will need a browser-grade fetcher, as creditas.cz returned 403 and the ČNB repository dropped the connection, neither of which should be read as dead.

Czech card acquiring and processing has an unusually good disclosure floor and an unusually poor press floor. The floor is statutory: every actor in this cell is a Czech legal entity obliged to file full annual accounts into the Sbírka listin, and ARES plus or.justice.cz resolve all of them cleanly and machine-readably — Global Payments Europe (IČO 27088936, the ex-MUZO Prague processing centre) and its separate acquiring arm Global Payments s.r.o. (04235452), Worldline Czech Republic (03633144, the entity behind the KB SmartPay joint venture with Komerční banka), Nexi Czech Republic (27391761), Comgate (27924505), MONET+ (26217783), Ingenico CZ (28869591) and Euronet Services (25608452). The press floor is weak because none of the three international processors maintains a Czech-language newsroom: Czech-specific announcements surface either in English at parent level (Global Payments IR, Worldline media relations and investors.worldline.com, Nexi /en/media-relations/), or through the domestic industry apparatus around Sdružení pro bankovní karty — bankovnikarty.cz statistics, the flat-file press archive at aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz/akt.htm, the CardMag trade magazine, and the Acquiring Day and Card Forum events — plus the ČTK wires Protext and České noviny. The sharpest and most under-exploited signals are contractual rather than editorial: KB SmartPay and Comgate publish dated, versioned merchant terms that make pricing changes datable, and the public contracts register together with the NEN procurement portal expose real acquiring contracts and award decisions naming winners and values.
